pearls: Epigastric pain initially (visceral peritoneal inflammation) that migrates to RLQ (parietal peritoneal inflammation).

topics.title: Polyp conditions
topics.summary: Q will tell you there’s a teenager (i.e., juvenile, LOL!) with intermittent bleeding per rectum + colonoscopy shows…
pearls: Q will tell you there’s a teenager (i.e., juvenile, LOL!) with intermittent bleeding per rectum + colonoscopy shows scattered polyps + biopsy shows “dilated, cystic, mucus-filled glands with abundant lamina propria and…
All you need to know is these are not pre-cancerous / have no dysplasia.
Dysplastic polyps that precede full-blown colorectal cancer are classically either tubular or villous, AND either pedunculated or sessile.

topics.title: Colon cancer short points
topics.summary: KRAS gene is the answer on USMLE for the first gene mutated in colonic polyps, prior to progression to overt colon …
pearls: KRAS gene is the answer on USMLE for the first gene mutated in colonic polyps, prior to progression to overt colon cancer.

Colon cancer often develops as a result of progressive mutations, rather than one mutation straight-up. In other words, first KRAS, then PTEN, then DCC, then TP53. This is a HY path point for some reason.
If they tell you a colon cancer has metastasized and force you to choose a gene that’s mutated, go with TP53 for p53 protein.

topics.title: Autoimmune intestinal absorptive disorders
topics.summary: Intolerance to gluten (i.e., to gliadin proteins found in wheat, oats, rye, and barley; but not rice).
pearls: Intolerance to gluten (i.e., to gliadin proteins found in wheat, oats, rye, and barley; but not rice).
Causes type-IV hypersensitivity response where T cells attack the small intestinal villi, resulting in flattening of the villi and malabsorption. The biopsy/image is pass-level.
D-xylose test is abnormal because the intestinal lining/architecture is abnormal (i.e., we have flattening of villi).

topics.title: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS)
topics.summary: Don’t confuse with IBD. IBS is psychosomatic (i.e., psych-related) condition.
pearls: Don’t confuse with IBD. IBS is psychosomatic (i.e., psych-related) condition.
Classic vignette will be a woman 20s-40s with stress factors who usually has alternating diarrhea / constipation; can also present as bloating or cramping.
Key detail is that symptoms are relieved with bowel motions.

topics.title: Obgyn-related hepatic issues
topics.summary: HELLP syndrome = Hemolysis, Elevated Liver enzymes, Low Platelet count.
pearls: HELLP syndrome = Hemolysis, Elevated Liver enzymes, Low Platelet count.
Can occur as part of severe preeclampsia (HTN + proteinuria after 20 weeks of pregnancy).
Vignette will be pregnant woman >20 weeks of pregnancy where you see the platelets and Hb are low and LFTs are up. Not complicated.

topics.title: Heavy metal liver diseases
topics.summary: Inability to secrete copper into bile from the liver. Copper is normally excreted by the body via secretion into bi…
pearls: Inability to secrete copper into bile from the liver. Copper is normally excreted by the body via secretion into bile.
↑ urinary copper + ↓ serum ceruloplasmin (copper-binding protein in the blood; in the case of copper overload, body tries to minimize amount carried in blood).

Buzzy / pass-level detail is Keiser-Fleischer rings, which is copper deposited in the cornea of the eye. Vignette can give you what sounds like Wilson disease, and then the answer is “slit-lamp exam.”

topics.title: Hepatocellular Carcinoma & Liver Mass Pathology
topics.summary: USMLE loves gross images of these conditions.
pearls: USMLE loves gross images of these conditions.
HCC will present as one large solitary lesion, sometimes with mini surrounding satellite lesions. Notice how the HCC is one solitary lesion. HCC can also grow as a “confluent multinodular” type.

Right heart failure (either due to cor pulmonale or CHF) can result in venous congestion within the liver. This can cause a characteristic mottled appearance on gross specimen known as “nutmeg liver.”

topics.title: Bowel ischemia
topics.summary: Patient with cardiovascular disease (CVD) + blood in the stool.
pearls: Patient with cardiovascular disease (CVD) + blood in the stool.
Caused by bleeding at ischemic ulcers at watershed areas in the colon (i.e., splenic flexure and rectosigmoid junction).
Can occur randomly or due to inciting event like recent AAA surgery.

pearls: L1 — - Supplies the midgut (2nd part of duodenum until 2/3 distal transverse colon). - What the USMLE will do is give vignette of SMA thrombosis in peripheral vascular disease, causing acute mesenteric ischemia, and then ask…

pearls: Enterotoxigenic E. coli causes traveler’s diarrhea.

pearls: S. aureus pre-formed heat-stable toxin is acquired from two main sources on NBME: 1) various meats sitting under a heat lamp / out for long periods of time, e.g., at a buffet; 2) dairy products like creams, custards, potato salad.

Notably causes vomiting 1-6 hours after consumption. This is notable, as the symptoms occur rather quickly. Diarrhea, both watery and bloody, can occur, but is not mandatory. The main crux is the vomiting.

pearls: Causes Whipple disease, a GI malabsorptive syndrome where the patient can also get arthritis and renal and cardiac disease.

100% of Qs will say “PAS-positive macrophages in the lamina propria.” You don’t need to know the image for this. But for whatever magical reason, the USMLE tests this detail. Old-school pathology docs who reminisce maybe.
Causes flattening of villi similar to Celiac, but considered infective/bacterial in origin. Literature says exact etiology not certain.

topics.summary: Most common cause of watery diarrhea in unvaccinated children < 5 years.
pearls: Most common cause of watery diarrhea in unvaccinated children < 5 years.
Vaccine normally given orally at 2, 4, and 6 months of age.
Double-stranded, segmented RNA (NBME asks it).

topics.summary: A protozoan is a unicellular eukaryote.
pearls: A protozoan is a unicellular eukaryote.

pearls: USMLE wants you to know routes of acquisition for the nematodes (i.e., ingested or through feet, etc.).

pearls: Fish tapeworm. Nothing else you need to know.

topics.title: Trematodes (flukes)
topics.summary: Penetrates skin when swimming; snail is host.
pearls: Penetrates skin when swimming; snail is host.

Ingested from crab meat or crayfish.

pearls: Shut of proton pumps on parietal cells → ↓ acid secretion.

Choose PPIs over H2 blockers for Tx of most things, like GERD, ulcers, and H. pylori.

topics.summary: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri) presents in young obese women with daily headache (which…
pearls: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri) presents in young obese women with daily headache (which worsens during the Valsalva maneuver), bilaterally symmetric papilledema, and transient visual disturbances.
Means increased intracranial pressure on USMLE.
Papilledema refers to blurring of the optic disc margins due inflammation of the optic nerve head in the setting of increased intracranial pressure. HY Autoimmune eye pathologies

topics.title: Retinoblastoma
topics.summary: Familial retinoblastoma occurs due to a germline mutation that affects the Rb tumor suppressor gene on chromosome 1…
pearls: Familial retinoblastoma occurs due to a germline mutation that affects the Rb tumor suppressor gene on chromosome 13; affected children carry one copy of the mutation in all their cells.

topics.title: Pupillary light reflex
topics.summary: The upper midbrain contains neural structures (eg, optic nerve, pretectal nuclei, Edinger-Westphal nuclei, oculomot…
pearls: The upper midbrain contains neural structures (eg, optic nerve, pretectal nuclei, Edinger-Westphal nuclei, oculomotor nerve) that mediate the direct and consensual pupillary light reflex.
The optic nerve carries the afferent limb of the pupillary light reflex pathway, which activates the efferent limb bilaterally and causes both direct and consensual pupillary constriction.

topics.title: Pupillary asymmetry ( aniscoria )
topics.summary: Pupillary asymmetry (ie, anisocoria) is caused by a lesion in the ocular parasympathetic (pupillary constriction) o…
pearls: Pupillary asymmetry (ie, anisocoria) is caused by a lesion in the ocular parasympathetic (pupillary constriction) or sympathetic (pupillary dilation) pathways.
In this patient, anisocoria increases in bright light, indicating that the larger right pupil is unable to constrict due to a defect in the right parasympathetic pathway.

topics.title: Mydriasis
topics.summary: Lesions of the intermediolateral cell column, or intermediate horn, between spinal cord levels C8 and T2 can interr…
pearls: Lesions of the intermediolateral cell column, or intermediate horn, between spinal cord levels C8 and T2 can interrupt the sympathetic nerve supply to the ipsilateral face and eye, and cause Horner syndrome.
This patient likely has a lesion of the ciliospinal center of Budge (labeled “B”)

topics.title: Horner syndrome
topics.summary: A tumor of the lung apex (Pancoast tumor) can compress both the brachial plexus and the stellate ganglion of the sy…
pearls: A tumor of the lung apex (Pancoast tumor) can compress both the brachial plexus and the stellate ganglion of the sympathetic chain (autonomic ganglion), leading to lower motor neuron arm weakness and ipsilateral Horner syndrome.

topics.title: Orbital Floor Fracture
topics.summary: Fractures to the orbital floor commonly result from direct frontal trauma to the orbit. The infraorbital nerve runs…
pearls: Fractures to the orbital floor commonly result from direct frontal trauma to the orbit. The infraorbital nerve runs along the orbital floor in a groove in the maxilla before exiting the skull just inferior to the orbit.

Blunt trauma to the globe can cause orbital blowout fractures. These fractures most commonly involve the medial or inferior orbital walls due to the thin bone bordering the ethmoid and maxillary sinuses.(Identify sinus on picture)

topics.title: Oculomotor Nerve
topics.summary: This patient has diplopia (suggesting a lesion impacting extraocular muscles) and a left efferent pupillary defect …
pearls: This patient has diplopia (suggesting a lesion impacting extraocular muscles) and a left efferent pupillary defect (absent left pupillary response when light enters either eye).

The oculomotor nerve (CN III) provides innervation to many of the extraocular muscles (superior rectus, medial rectus, inferior rectus, inferior oblique), parasympathetic innervation to the pupil, and somatic innervation of the…
Superior orbital fissure — - Efferent component of light reflex (constricts pupil via parasympathetic innervation).

topics.title: Trochlear nerve
topics.summary: The trochlear nerve innervates the superior oblique muscle, which causes the eye to intort (internally rotate) and …
pearls: The trochlear nerve innervates the superior oblique muscle, which causes the eye to intort (internally rotate) and depress while adducted.
Superior orbital fissure — - Innervates superior oblique (eye looks inferomedially).

topics.title: The abducens nerve (CN VI)
topics.summary: The abducens nerve (CN VI) innervates the lateral rectus muscle, which originates at the annular tendon and inserts…
pearls: The abducens nerve (CN VI) innervates the lateral rectus muscle, which originates at the annular tendon and inserts on the temporal (ie, lateral) surface of the globe. It functions to abduct the eye.
The arrow in the below CT scan points to an extraocular muscle that originates at the annular tendon and inserts onto the temporal (ie, lateral) surface of the globe.
Superior orbital fissure — - Abducts eye (patient gazes laterally).

topics.title: Visual field defects
topics.summary: After traversing the lateral geniculate nucleus, visual information travels to the primary visual cortex in the occ…
pearls: After traversing the lateral geniculate nucleus, visual information travels to the primary visual cortex in the occipital lobe by way of the optic radiations.
Superior optic radiations carry information from the superior retina/inferior visual field.

topics.title: Cavernous sinus
topics.summary: This patient has a cavernous carotid aneurysm, which was discovered during an evaluation for a change in headache f…
pearls: This patient has a cavernous carotid aneurysm, which was discovered during an evaluation for a change in headache frequency and severity from past migraines.
Infection of the medial face, sinuses (ethmoidal or sphenoidal), or teeth may spread through the valveless facial venous system into the cavernous sinus, resulting in cavernous sinus thrombosis.
Severe headache, diplopia, proptosis, and/or ophthalmoplegia in patient with recent sinus infection.

topics.title: Internuclear ophthalmoplegia
topics.summary: Internuclear ophthalmoplegia is a disorder of impaired horizontal gaze caused by a lesion in the medial longitudina…
pearls: Internuclear ophthalmoplegia is a disorder of impaired horizontal gaze caused by a lesion in the medial longitudinal fasciculus (MLF).

topics.title: NEU High-Yield Synthesis
topics.summary: Anterior chamber: Fluid-filled space between the cornea and iris; contains aqueous humor, a clear fluid that nouris…
pearls: Anterior chamber: Fluid-filled space between the cornea and iris; contains aqueous humor, a clear fluid that nourishes the cornea and maintains intraocular pressure.
Chronic eye condition characterized by increased intraocular pressure due to impaired drainage of aqueous humor.
Unlike acute angle-closure (closed-angle) glaucoma, the drainage angle (canal of Schlemm) between the cornea and iris remains open.

topics.title: UV light-induced Ophthal pathologies
topics.summary: Melanomas can grow from the conjunctiva and cornea. Just be aware they exist.
pearls: Melanomas can grow from the conjunctiva and cornea. Just be aware they exist.
Non-cancerous overgrowth of non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium growing from the conjunctiva.
Crosses over the cornea (clear part of the eye covering the iris and pupil).

topics.title: Miscellaneous hereditary conditions
topics.summary: USMLE wants you to know that mitochondrial disorders, e.g., LHON, present as a triad of 1) eye/ear problems, 2) hyp…
pearls: USMLE wants you to know that mitochondrial disorders, e.g., LHON, present as a triad of 1) eye/ear problems, 2) hypotonia, and 3) lactic acidosis (low bicarb; metabolic acidosis).
Other mitochondrial disorder names you could be aware of are MELAS (Mitochondrial Encephalopathy, Lactic Acidosis, and Stroke-like episodes) and MERRF (Myoclonic epilepsy with ragged red fibers).
Heteroplasmy is variability of phenotype severity across offspring (Step 1 term).

topics.title: Ophthalmia neonatorum
topics.summary: Fancy way of saying neonatal conjunctivitis.
pearls: Fancy way of saying neonatal conjunctivitis.
Caused by C. trachomatis D-K (the STD).

Presents usually >1 week post-birth and can lead to pneumonia with a lymphocytic shift (since chlamydia is obligate intracellular, so requires lymphocytes for cell-mediated immunity to clear them, unlike extracellular bacteria…

topics.title: Herpesviridae infections
topics.summary: Keratitis is inflammation of the cornea.
pearls: Keratitis is inflammation of the cornea.
HSV1/2 can cause dendritic (tree-like) pattern in the eye on fluorescein instillation.
May or may not cause vesicles around the eye as well.

topics.title: Stroke risk factors
topics.summary: The two most important risk factors for stroke (cerebral infarction) on USMLE are hypertension and atrial fibrillat…
pearls: The two most important risk factors for stroke (cerebral infarction) on USMLE are hypertension and atrial fibrillation.

Regarding HTN, a strong systolic impulse pounds the carotid arteries, leading to endothelial damage and increased development of atherosclerotic plaques (carotid stenosis), which then launch off to the brain/eye.
Atrial fibrillation results in turbulence and stasis, leading to left atrial mural thrombus, which launches off.

topics.title: Other stroke syndromes
topics.summary: The answer for ipsilateral Bells palsy after a stroke.
pearls: The answer for ipsilateral Bells palsy after a stroke.
Due to stroke of anterior inferior cerebellar artery (AICA).
FACIAL (contains AICA backwards) → “That’s the one that’s Bells palsy.”

topics.title: Lenticulostriate strokes
topics.summary: HTN can cause lipohyalinosis (fancy word for microatheroma formation) of small lenticulostriate arteries deep withi…
pearls: HTN can cause lipohyalinosis (fancy word for microatheroma formation) of small lenticulostriate arteries deep within the brain.
Ischemia within these small vessels leads to necrosis and reabsorption of tissue, leading to tiny cavities called lacunae.
Unlike larger strokes, lacunar infarcts often do not present with cortical deficits like aphasia, neglect, or visual field losses.

topics.title: Neuro necrosis points (Step 1 only)
topics.summary: Liquefactive necrosis is the answer for necrosis of nervous system tissue.
pearls: Liquefactive necrosis is the answer for necrosis of nervous system tissue.
“Red neurons” is the answer for what will be seen acutely with ischemic infarction of the CNS. This refers to their strong eosinophilic (pink) staining with H&E.
Microglia are the resident macrophages of the CNS. They phagocytose necrotic brain/spinal tissue.

topics.title: Aphasia types
topics.summary: Fluent aphasia (i.e., patient can speak with normal pace + use lots of words), but none of it makes sense (“word sa…
pearls: Fluent aphasia (i.e., patient can speak with normal pace + use lots of words), but none of it makes sense (“word salad”).
Ability to comprehend is similarly impaired (i.e., patient makes no sense in terms of what comes out + inability to make any sense of what comes in).
Repetition is impaired (i.e., patient cannot repeat back a sentence spoken to him/her).

topics.title: Stroke management / Tx
topics.summary: Do not give tPA. First step is lowering BP (labetalol, nicardipine, or hydralazine).
pearls: Do not give tPA. First step is lowering BP (labetalol, nicardipine, or hydralazine).
Reduce BP rapidly to systolic <140 mm Hg.
Reverse anticoagulation if the patient is on it (i.e., FFP for patients on warfarin).

topics.title: Sodium correction
topics.summary: Correcting hyponatremia too quickly with hypertonic saline causes central pontine myelinolysis.
pearls: Correcting hyponatremia too quickly with hypertonic saline causes central pontine myelinolysis.
Can be described as “osmotic demyelination.”
Causes locked-in syndrome.

topics.title: Hypercalcemic crisis
topics.summary: Refers to cognitive dysfunction / a delirium-like state in the setting of severe hypercalcemia, often due to malign…
pearls: Refers to cognitive dysfunction / a delirium-like state in the setting of severe hypercalcemia, often due to malignancy or primary hyperparathyroidism.
USMLE wants you to know that high calcium, as well as any sodium disturbance, can cause delirium.
First step on USMLE for Tx of hypercalcemia is normal saline.

topics.title: Spinal conditions
topics.summary: Loss of dorsal columns due to neurosyphilis.
pearls: Loss of dorsal columns due to neurosyphilis.
Cyan dot marks the anterior white commissure.
Maybe 1/3 of Qs will also involve corticospinal tract, where you’ll see some impaired motor function in addition to the bilateral loss of pain/temperature.

topics.title: Brachial plexus injuries
topics.summary: Both can be caused in neonates by breech / traumatic labor.
pearls: Both can be caused in neonates by breech / traumatic labor.
Can also be caused by injuries such as grabbing onto tree branch while falling.
Lower brachial plexus injury (C8-T1).

topics.title: Spina bifida
topics.summary: Meningocele: Neural tube defect with herniation of just the meninges through the vertebral arch.
pearls: Meningocele: Neural tube defect with herniation of just the meninges through the vertebral arch.
Meningomyelocele: Neural tube defect with herniation of the meninges + spinal cord through the vertebral arch.
HY point is that neural tube defects (spina bifida) occur between 3-4 weeks gestation.

topics.title: Lower limb nerve HY Points
topics.summary: The answer on USMLE if patient loses both eversion and dorsiflexion of the foot.
pearls: The answer on USMLE if patient loses both eversion and dorsiflexion of the foot.
Sensation to upper third of lateral leg (around and below lateral knee).
Splits into superficial and deep peroneal (fibular) nerves.

topics.title: Neurogenic joint
topics.summary: Aka Charcot joint, where patient injures joint due to lack of joint sensation from peripheral neuropathy.
pearls: Aka Charcot joint, where patient injures joint due to lack of joint sensation from peripheral neuropathy.
Usually seen in diabetes; can also be seen in neurosyphilis.
The answer on USMLE when they say diabetic patient has “disorganization of the tarsometatarsal joints” on foot x-ray. Upper limb nerve HY Points for USMLE

topics.title: Mononeuritis multiplex
topics.summary: Weird neuropathy that means neuropathy of “one large nerve in many locations” – e.g., wrist drop + foot drop in sam…
pearls: Weird neuropathy that means neuropathy of “one large nerve in many locations” – e.g., wrist drop + foot drop in same patient.
Presents in patients with one of the vasculitides (i.e., Wegener, Churg-Strauss, microscopic polyangiitis).
Formerly known as Wegener granulomatosis.

topics.title: dementia types
topics.summary: Aka Pick disease.
pearls: Presents usually as triad of 1) personality change, 2) apathy, and 3) disinhibition.

Accumulation of hyperphosphorylated tau protein (similar to Alzheimer), except rather than accumulating as neurofibrillary tangles, it accumulates as round, silver- staining inclusions knowns as Pick bodies.
Dementia + visual hallucinations + Parkinsonism.

topics.title: Optic neuritis
topics.summary: Inflammation of CN II (optic nerve).
pearls: Inflammation of CN II (optic nerve).
Presents variably as change in visual acuity, color vision, central scotoma, etc.
Basically synonymous with multiple sclerosis on USMLE. I discuss MS more later.

topics.title: Myoneural junction disorders
topics.summary: Autoantibodies against post-synaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors.
pearls: Autoantibodies against post-synaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors.
Classic vignette is female office worker in her 40s who has triad of 1) diplopia, 2) dysphagia/hoarseness, and 3) ptosis that worsens throughout the day.
Gets worse with recurrent stimulation of muscle (vignette might say the patient cannot perform upward gaze for 60 seconds).

topics.title: headache types
topics.summary: Prophylaxis is verapamil.
pearls: Prophylaxis is verapamil.
Tx for acute episodes is oxygen (bizarre, unless patient has O2 tank lying around).
Aka giant cell arteritis.

topics.title: WKS and ataxia
topics.summary: Ataxia means lack of coordination of voluntary muscles presenting as unsteady gait and balance.
pearls: Ataxia means lack of coordination of voluntary muscles presenting as unsteady gait and balance.
Damage to primarily the mamillary bodies due to thiamine (B1) deficiency.
Wernicke encephalopathy = A COW = Ataxia/Anterograde amnesia, Confusion, Ophthalmoplegia, Wernicke.

topics.title: Cerebellar lesion signs
topics.summary: Aka “hepatic flap.” Seen in liver disease.
pearls: Aka “hepatic flap.” Seen in liver disease.
Motor disturbance characterized by brief, sudden lapses of muscle tone, presenting as the patient demonstrating a “flapping” motion of the hands when he or she extends the arms and hands anteriorly.
Impaired ability to perform rapid alternating movements, presenting as difficulty rapidly tapping a finger or quickly pronating and supinating the hand.

topics.title: Neuro conditions caused by vitamin deficiencies
topics.summary: As discussed earlier, causes subacute combined degeneration, with reversible dementia and/or systemic neurologic fi…
pearls: As discussed earlier, causes subacute combined degeneration, with reversible dementia and/or systemic neurologic findings.
Hx of gastrectomy, pernicious anemia, veganism, or strict vegetarianism is buzzy.

If patient has B12 deficiency + an unrelated autoimmune disorder, e.g., vitiligo, Hashimoto, etc., the cause is probably pernicious anemia, since “autoimmune diseases go together,” where having one autoimmune disease ↑ risk of…

topics.title: Tremor types
topics.summary: Autosomal dominant intention tremor.
pearls: Autosomal dominant intention tremor.
Can occur at any age, but usually middle age and older.
Patients self-medicate with alcohol, which ↓ tremor.

topics.title: Meningitis
topics.summary: Presents as high fever + stiff neck and photophobia.
pearls: Presents as high fever + stiff neck and photophobia.
In neonates: Group B Strep (Strep agalactiae; gram-positive cocci) most common. Can also be Listeria (gram-positive rods) or E. coli (gram-negative rods).
Everyone else (not neonates): S. pneumo (gram-positive diplococci) and N. meningitides (gram-negative diplococci) most common.

topics.title: Encephalitis
topics.summary: Presents as high fever + confusion.
pearls: Presents as high fever + confusion.
Herpes encephalitis can occur following vertical transmission in neonates. Can also be previously young healthy adults.
RBCs in the CSF due to temporal lobe hemorrhage.

topics.title: Neuropathic pain disorders
topics.summary: Presents as pain, paresthesia, and/or numbness in diabetic.
pearls: Presents as pain, paresthesia, and/or numbness in diabetic.
USMLE likes TCAs (i.e., amitriptyline) or gabapentin as first-line for Tx.
Use nortriptyline in elderly if a TCA is given (fewer side-effects).

topics.title: Cutaneous nerve endings + what they detect
topics.summary: The answer for deep pressure and vibration.
pearls: The answer for deep pressure and vibration.
The answer for light touch and vibration.
The answer for detecting shapes and textures.

topics.title: TNR + Prion disorders
topics.summary: Autosomal dominant; CAG trinucleotide repeat (TNR) expansion on chromosome 4 resulting in neurodegeneration and cho…
pearls: Autosomal dominant; CAG trinucleotide repeat (TNR) expansion on chromosome 4 resulting in neurodegeneration and choreoathetosis.
Chorea = fast, purposeless, jerky movements; athetosis = slow, writhing movements.
Anticipation = disorder occurs earlier and more severe with each successive generation; caused by expansion of the TNR repeat.

topics.title: Infective neuropathies
topics.summary: RNA virus that infects the anterior horns of the spinal cord and causes polio myelitis (inflammation of spinal cord…
pearls: RNA virus that infects the anterior horns of the spinal cord and causes polio myelitis (inflammation of spinal cord).
Classically causes degeneration of motor neurons in one leg, leading to one leg much smaller than the other leg.
Highest yield points about Polio actually have zero to do with the infection and almost all to do with the vaccines.

topics.title: Toxin-induced neuropathies
topics.summary: Causes flaccid paralysis.
pearls: Causes flaccid paralysis.
Botulin toxin of Clostridium botulinum inhibits presynaptic SNARE protein, resulting in ↓ release of presynaptic acetylcholine, which is normally stimulatory at muscles.
Botulism on USMLE can present as constipation, hypotonia, and cranial nerve palsies.

topics.title: Narcolepsy
topics.summary: Chronic sleep disorder affecting the brain’s ability to regulate sleep-wake cycles normally.
pearls: Chronic sleep disorder affecting the brain’s ability to regulate sleep-wake cycles normally.

Characterized by excessive daytime sleepiness, sudden episodes of muscle weakness (cataplexy), sleep paralysis, and hallucinations. The latter tend to occur prior to sleep (hypnagogic) or upon waking up (hypnopompic).
Thought to be due to deficiency of a neurotransmitter called orexin (aka hypocretin), which normally promotes wakefulness.

topics.title: Cushing reflex
topics.summary: Cushing reflex is a triad seen with ↑ ICP, where the patient will have: 1) HTN, 2) bradycardia, and 3) respiratory …
pearls: Cushing reflex is a triad seen with ↑ ICP, where the patient will have: 1) HTN, 2) bradycardia, and 3) respiratory disturbance (classically ↓ RR, but there’s an NBME Q where they don’t give RR as ↓).
The ↓ RR is due to ↑ ICP causing compression of brainstem.
It’s to my observation across NBME exams that they will never ask you to formally calculate GCS score.

topics.title: CNS malignancy
topics.summary: Can present with seizure and/or morning vomiting (a sign of ↑ ICP).
pearls: Can present with seizure and/or morning vomiting (a sign of ↑ ICP).
Can be described as ring-enhancing lesions (i.e., this descriptor is not limited to Toxo; it can also be tumors/metastases and abscesses). Peds brain tumors
Can cause vertical gaze palsy in kids (Parinaud syndrome).

topics.title: Adult brain tumors
topics.summary: Most common pituitary tumor in adults.
pearls: Most common pituitary tumor in adults.
Can cause amenorrhea in women and impotence in men.
Galactorrhea can occur in everyone.

topics.title: Tic disorders
topics.summary: Neurologic disorder characterized by repetitive, involuntary movements and vocalizations (i.e., tics).
pearls: Neurologic disorder characterized by repetitive, involuntary movements and vocalizations (i.e., tics).
Motor tics range from mere eye blinking, head jerking, or shoulder shrugging to more complex movements such as hopping, twirling, or even mimicking others' actions.
Vocal (phonic) tics include throat clearing, sniffing, or humming. More complex vocal tics can involve repeating words or phrases, or shouting inappropriate words (coprolalia).

topics.title: Seizure terminology
topics.summary: Focal-onset aware seizure (FOAS).
pearls: Focal-onset aware seizure (FOAS).
Formerly known as simple seizures.
No loss of consciousness (LoC).

topics.title: Epilepsy disorders
topics.summary: Most common epilepsy disorder. Originates at the medial temporal lobe.
pearls: Most common epilepsy disorder. Originates at the medial temporal lobe.
Seizures are often preceded by visual auras, or warning signs. These can manifest as gustatory/olfactory sensations or déj→ vu.
FOIAS are most common type, with or without secondary generalization.

topics.title: Phakomatoses (neurocutaneous disorders)
topics.summary: NF1; AD; chromosome 17.
pearls: NF1; AD; chromosome 17.
Neurofibromas, café au lait spots (hyperpigmented macules), axillary/groin freckling, Lisch nodules (iris hamartomas), pheochromocytoma, optic nerve glioma, oligodendroglioma, ependymoma.
NF2; AD; chromosome 22.

topics.title: Lysosomal storage diseases
topics.summary: All are associated with cognitive/neurologic deficits.
pearls: All are associated with cognitive/neurologic deficits.
AR except for Fabry and Hunter, which are XR.

N-acetylglucosamine- 1-phosphotransferase — Many lysosomal enzymes — - Cannot synthesize mannose-6-phosphate at the Golgi; M6P needed to target lysosomal enzymes to the lysosomes; instead, lysosomal enzymes are secreted into…

topics.title: Extraocular nerve palsies
topics.summary: Superior orbital fissure — - Afferent component of corneal reflex.
pearls: Superior orbital fissure — - Afferent component of corneal reflex.
Foramen Rotundum — - Trigeminal mnemonic: “Standing Room Only.”
Foramen Ovale — - Muscles of mastication.

topics.title: Rinne + Weber tests
topics.summary: A vibrating tuning fork is placed against the mastoid bone (bone conduction; BC). Once the patient can no longer he…
pearls: A vibrating tuning fork is placed against the mastoid bone (bone conduction; BC). Once the patient can no longer hear it, it is removed from the bone and placed in front of the ear canal (air conduction; AC).
For both normal hearing and sensorineural hearing loss, AC > BC.
For conductive hearing loss, BC > AC.

topics.title: Muscarinic receptor antagonists
topics.summary: Classic textbook drug that blocks muscarinic receptors.
pearls: Classic textbook drug that blocks muscarinic receptors.
Can be used to increase heart rate during surgery.
Given as 1st -line Tx for organophosphate poisoning before pralidoxime.

topics.title: Depolarizing nicotinic receptor agonist (acts as antagonist)
topics.summary: Functions as antagonist due to desensitization of receptors.
pearls: Functions as antagonist due to desensitization of receptors.
Binds to nicotinic receptors and agonizes them, causing initial action potentials and muscle twitching (fasciculations), prior to desensitization and muscle paralysis.
Akin to leuprolide causing desensitization of GnRH receptors with continued binding, where despite being a GnRH receptor agonist, it acts functionally as an antagonist.

topics.title: Smoking cessation agents
topics.summary: Dopamine + norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor; has anti-depressant effects.
pearls: Dopamine + norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor; has anti-depressant effects.
Also antagonizes nicotinic receptors, which disincentivizes smoking, since doing so won’t produce rewarding effects.
Lowers seizure threshold. Don’t give to patients with eating disorders (electrolyte abnormalities increase seizure risk).

topics.title: Epilepsy/hypnotic agents
topics.summary: USMLE doesn’t care about MOAs for these. They care about side-effects mostly, as per my observation.
pearls: USMLE doesn’t care about MOAs for these. They care about side-effects mostly, as per my observation.
Blocks sodium channels.
Generic anti-epileptic; also used as prophylaxis for trigeminal neuralgia.

topics.title: Parkinson drugs
topics.summary: Ropinirole, pramipexole, cabergoline, pergolide, and bromocriptine.
pearls: Ropinirole, pramipexole, cabergoline, pergolide, and bromocriptine.
Used for Parkinson disease management.
Bromocriptine classic agent used for prolactinoma (dopamine agonism ↓ prolactin).

topics.title: Alzheimer drugs
topics.summary: As mentioned earlier, this is a cholinesterase inhibitor used in Alzheimer.
pearls: As mentioned earlier, this is a cholinesterase inhibitor used in Alzheimer.
Rivastigmine and galantamine you can be aware of and have same MOA, but are LY.
NMDA glutamate receptor antagonist.

topics.title: Quick anesthetics garbage
topics.summary: Mean alveolar concentration.
pearls: Mean alveolar concentration.
Used to determine the potency of inhaled anesthetics.
Dose of inhaled anesthetic required to prevent movement in 50% of patients to external noxious stimuli.

topics.title: Inhaled anesthetics
topics.summary: All used for general anesthesia (i.e., to put the patient to sleep).
pearls: All used for general anesthesia (i.e., to put the patient to sleep).
All potentiate GABA + inhibit NMDA glutamate receptors.
Can cause malignant hyperthermia (same as succinylcholine).

topics.title: Intravenous anesthetics
topics.summary: Often used in trauma situations for procedural sedation.
pearls: Often used in trauma situations for procedural sedation.
Classic agent used to maintain general anesthesia.
White in color (looks like milk).

topics.title: Neurotoxic drugs
topics.summary: Prevents microtubule assembly; used as general chemotherapy.
pearls: Prevents microtubule assembly; used as general chemotherapy.
USMLE can ask what drug inhibits and answer is just “tubulin.”
Peripheral / autonomic neuropathy.

topics.title: Neuroanatomy & Cranial Lesion Synthesis
topics.summary: 59F + metastatic cancer + in pain + crying + “wants to die”; Q asks most likely reason for wanting to die; answer =…
pearls: 59F + metastatic cancer + in pain + crying + “wants to die”; Q asks most likely reason for wanting to die; answer = “inadequate pain control”; “major depression” is wrong answer; must address pain management in cancer patients.
Frontal lobe injury in car accident; NBME asks which deficit is most likely to ensue; answer = conceptual planning.
Tx of nacrolepsy = stimulants (i.e., modafinil).

topics.title: Neuropathology & Special Senses Pearls
topics.summary: First learn:
pearls: How does the pons tend to appear on the Step 1 NBME/USMLE?

topics.title: Atrophy
topics.summary: This patient experienced decreased physical workload when his leg was immobilized. As a result, the skeletal muscle…
pearls: This patient experienced decreased physical workload when his leg was immobilized. As a result, the skeletal muscle fibers in his leg decreased in size, leading to disuse atrophy.
Metabolically inactive muscle experiences disuse atrophy through the loss of trophic signals from stretch, reflex, and load bearing.
Diminished cell growth/size due to under-stimulation.

topics.title: Metaplasia
topics.summary: Metaplasia is the substitution of one differentiated cell type for another due to the presence of an adverse enviro…
pearls: Metaplasia is the substitution of one differentiated cell type for another due to the presence of an adverse environmental stimulus.
Squamous bronchial metaplasia is a reversible, adaptive response to chronic irritation, such as smoking.
Tissue/organ doesn’t develop.

pearls: The majority of CO2 produced in the tissues is transported to the lungs as bicarbonate ion (HCO3−). Within red blood cells (RBCs), the enzyme carbonic anhydrase forms HCO3− from CO2 and water.
Carbonic anhydrase is an enzyme present in erythrocytes that catalyzes the formation of bicarbonate from water and carbon dioxide.

pearls: Fibrotic thickening of the interstitial space (between the air and blood) increases the distance that oxygen must cross, limiting the degree of oxygen diffusion.
This patient has an acute benzodiazepine overdose. Acute benzodiazepine (eg, alprazolam, lorazepam) overdose causes central respiratory depression with hypoventilation.

topics.title: Hemoglobin

pearls: Deoxyhemoglobin is a better buffer of hydrogen ions than oxyhemoglobin, which explains why deoxygenated blood can carry more carbon dioxide for a given Pco2 than oxygenated blood.

pearls: Oxygen (O2) is carried in the blood, both as a dissolved gas and in combination with hemoglobin.
The laboratory studies in this case indicates a reduced arterial and venous oxygen content.

pearls: A left shift of the hemoglobin oxygen dissociation curve indicates increased hemoglobin O2 affinity and can be caused by increased pH, decreased 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate, and decreased temperature.

P50 refers to the partial pressure of oxygen at which hemoglobin is 50% saturated. Hemoglobins with high oxygen affinity have a decreased P50 that is represented by a leftward shift of the oxygen dissociation curve.

topics.title: Response to High altitude
topics.summary: At high altitude, the low partial pressure of inspired oxygen (PiO2) leads to hypoxemia that triggers hyperventilat…
pearls: At high altitude, the low partial pressure of inspired oxygen (PiO2) leads to hypoxemia that triggers hyperventilation with increased exhalation of CO2 and resulting respiratory alkalosis.

The hypoxemia and alkalemia can cause symptoms of altitude sickness (eg, headache, fatigue, lightheadedness). The kidneys respond by creating a compensatory metabolic acidosis and by increasing erythropoietin secretion.

topics.title: Response to exercise
topics.summary: Physiologic changes in the respiratory system that occur with exercise include increased minute ventilation (via bo…
pearls: Physiologic changes in the respiratory system that occur with exercise include increased minute ventilation (via both an increase in respiratory rate and tidal volume), reduced physiologic dead space, increased…
During physical exercise, there is increased skeletal muscle CO2 production that increases the CO2 content of venous blood.

topics.title: Aging
topics.summary: Aging is associated with steady decreases in chest wall compliance but increases in lung compliance due to a loss o…
pearls: Aging is associated with steady decreases in chest wall compliance but increases in lung compliance due to a loss of elastic recoil.
Diminished elastic recoil and the collapse of supporting tissues around the airways cause a significant increase in residual volume (RV).

topics.title: Methemoglobin

pearls: This patient with cyanosis that does not improve with supplemental oxygen has acquired methemoglobinemia due to the topical anesthetic (ie, benzocaine).

With iron in the oxidized ferric state, methemoglobin is unable to bind oxygen. In addition, the affinity of any residual ferrous iron in the hemoglobin tetramer is increased, causing a leftward shift of the oxygen-dissociation…

topics.title: Cyanide Toxicity
topics.summary: Cyanide is a potent mitochondrial toxin that binds heme centers in cytochrome c oxidase (complex IV), blocking the …
pearls: Cyanide is a potent mitochondrial toxin that binds heme centers in cytochrome c oxidase (complex IV), blocking the electron transport chain.
This patient's clinical presentation is consistent with cyanide toxicity from nitroprusside.

topics.title: Carbon monoxide
topics.summary: Carbon monoxide binds heme iron in hemoglobin with an affinity much greater than oxygen, generating carboxyhemoglob…
pearls: Carbon monoxide binds heme iron in hemoglobin with an affinity much greater than oxygen, generating carboxyhemoglobin.
CO poisoning increases carboxyhemoglobin concentrations but does not affect the partial pressure of oxygen and does not precipitate methemoglobinemia.

topics.title: Epistaxis
topics.summary: Epistaxis is commonly caused by irritation of the highly vascular mucosa at the anterior nasal septum. The anterior…
pearls: Epistaxis is commonly caused by irritation of the highly vascular mucosa at the anterior nasal septum. The anterior nasal septum contains the Kiesselbach plexus.

topics.title: Head and neck cancer
topics.summary: The eustachian tube connects the middle ear to the nasopharynx. Cancer located in the nasopharynx can lead to obstr…
pearls: The eustachian tube connects the middle ear to the nasopharynx. Cancer located in the nasopharynx can lead to obstruction of the eustachian tube, causing a middle ear effusion.
Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma is likely in a patient with cervical adenopathy and a base of tongue mass, especially with a history of tobacco use.

topics.title: Pulmonary emboli
topics.summary: The combination of calf swelling, history of prolonged immobility, and sudden-onset dyspnea is strongly suggestive …
pearls: The combination of calf swelling, history of prolonged immobility, and sudden-onset dyspnea is strongly suggestive of acute pulmonary embolism (PE).
Ventilation/perfusion scanning can be useful for diagnosing pulmonary embolism. A large perfusion defect without ventilation defect is the characteristic positive test result.
DVT that has embolized up the venous circulation to the pulmonary arteries.

topics.title: Fat embolism syndrome
topics.summary: Fat embolism syndrome should be strongly suspected in a patient with severe long-bone and/or pelvic fractures who d…
pearls: Fat embolism syndrome should be strongly suspected in a patient with severe long-bone and/or pelvic fractures who develops acute-onset neurologic abnormalities, hypoxemia, and a petechial rash.
Fat embolism syndrome most commonly results from the release of fat globules from bone marrow following a long-bone or pelvic fracture.
The answer on USMLE if they say long-bone fracture (i.e., usually femur) in patient who now develops shortness of breath + petechiae on the shoulders/chest.

topics.title: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
topics.summary: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease involves components of chronic bronchitis and emphysema. Bronchial airway obs…
pearls: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease involves components of chronic bronchitis and emphysema.
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease causes air trapping and hyperinflation; consequently, these patients breathe at higher baseline lung volumes (higher functional residual capacity).
COPD = chronic bronchitis + emphysema.

topics.title: Chronic bronchitis
topics.summary: Thickened bronchial walls, lymphocytic infiltration, mucous gland enlargement, and patchy squamous metaplasia of th…
pearls: Thickened bronchial walls, lymphocytic infiltration, mucous gland enlargement, and patchy squamous metaplasia of the bronchial mucosa are features of chronic bronchitis.
Hyperplasia of the submucosal bronchial glands is the major contributor to bronchial wall thickening in chronic bronchitis.
Chronic bronchitis = productive cough for at least 3 months in a year, for 2+ years.

topics.title: Asthma
topics.summary: This patient's intermittent respiratory symptoms (eg, dyspnea, cough) in the setting of a normal chest x-ray, sputu…
pearls: This patient's intermittent respiratory symptoms (eg, dyspnea, cough) in the setting of a normal chest x-ray, sputum eosinophils, and reduced FEV1 (<80% predicted) are highly suggestive of asthma.
Occupational asthma is characterized by airway inflammation, bronchial hyperreactivity, and a variable airflow obstruction triggered by workplace exposure.
Bronchospasm that occurs either idiopathically/hereditarily, or in response to certain allergens or cold air.

topics.title: Inhaled B2 agonists
topics.summary: Asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation are the most frequent causes of pulsus paradox…
pearls: Asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation are the most frequent causes of pulsus paradoxus in the absence of significant pericardial disease.
Short-acting beta-2 agonists (eg, albuterol, levalbuterol) are hydrophilic and are rapidly metabolized, explaining their rapid onset and short duration of action.

topics.title: Inhaled and oral glucocorticoids
topics.summary: Asthma is characterized by chronic airway inflammation, which leads to airway remodeling, airway hyperresponsivenes…
pearls: Asthma is characterized by chronic airway inflammation, which leads to airway remodeling, airway hyperresponsiveness, and bronchoconstriction.
Corticosteroids (eg, fluticasone, budesonide) have multiple beneficial effects in the treatment of asthma.

topics.title: Muscarinic antagonists

pearls: Ipratropium, an anticholinergic agent and derivative of atropine, treats obstructive lung disease by blocking acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors, which prevents bronchoconstriction and reduces mucus secretion from…

topics.title: Antileukotriens
topics.summary: Leukotriene receptor antagonists work by inhibiting binding of leukotrienes to the leukotriene receptor, a G protei…
pearls: Leukotriene receptor antagonists work by inhibiting binding of leukotrienes to the leukotriene receptor, a G protein-coupled receptor.

The cysteinyl-containing leukotrienes (ie, leukotriene C4, D4, and E4) are inflammatory mediators that stimulate bronchoconstriction, bronchial mucus secretion, and bronchial edema to contribute to the pathogenesis of asthma.

topics.title: IgE-binding monoclonal antibodies (eg, omalizumab)
topics.summary: IgE-binding monoclonal antibodies (eg, omalizumab) are effective in treating asthma that remains uncontrolled despi…
pearls: IgE-binding monoclonal antibodies (eg, omalizumab) are effective in treating asthma that remains uncontrolled despite optimal therapy with bronchodilators and inhaled corticosteroids.
Monoclonal antibody against IgE.
Can be used in theory in severe asthmatics who have high IgE levels.

topics.title: Methylxanthines
topics.summary: Theophylline (Methylxanthines) is an adenosine receptor antagonist and indirect adrenergic agent with a narrow ther…
pearls: Theophylline (Methylxanthines) is an adenosine receptor antagonist and indirect adrenergic agent with a narrow therapeutic index. It is predominantly metabolized by the hepatic cytochrome oxidases.

topics.title: Cromolyn
topics.summary: Cromolyn and nedocromil are mast cell-stabilizing agents that inhibit mast cell degranulation independent of the tr…
pearls: Cromolyn and nedocromil are mast cell-stabilizing agents that inhibit mast cell degranulation independent of the triggering stimulus.
Mast cell stabilizers used for asthma. Prevent release of histamine.

topics.title: Bronchiectasis
topics.summary: Cystic fibrosis is an autosomal recessive disorder in which a defective chloride channel causes impaired clearance …
pearls: Cystic fibrosis is an autosomal recessive disorder in which a defective chloride channel causes impaired clearance of thick, viscous airway secretions.
Pulmonary function testing in cystic fibrosis reveals an obstructive pattern, characterized by a decreased FEV1/FVC ratio and an increased total lung capacity and residual volume.
Dilation of the airways (ectasia means dilation) that occurs due to “loss of musculature of the airways.”

topics.title: Restrictive lung diseases
topics.summary: The pathogenesis of IPF is thought to be driven by repetitive epithelial injury (eg, smoking, acid reflux) followed…
pearls: The pathogenesis of IPF is thought to be driven by repetitive epithelial injury (eg, smoking, acid reflux) followed by disordered repair:

topics.summary: This young patient presenting with respiratory symptoms and central obesity without a history of pulmonary disease …
pearls: This young patient presenting with respiratory symptoms and central obesity without a history of pulmonary disease likely has obesity-related restrictive lung disease.
The most common indicator of obesity-related disease is a reduction in expiratory reserve volume (ERV), which is the maximum volume of air that can be expired after a normal tidal expiration.

topics.title: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis
topics.summary: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis results from an exaggerated immunologic response to an inhaled antigen (eg, mold, anim…
pearls: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis results from an exaggerated immunologic response to an inhaled antigen (eg, mold, animal protein), and presents with cough and dyspnea of variable acuity.
Answer on USMLE for bilateral lung condition + fever in farmer who has exposure to hay (on new Step 1 NBME).
They will tell you the fever self-resolves after 2 days and he now is afebrile.

topics.title: Sarcoidosis
topics.summary: Sarcoidosis is an inflammatory disorder characterized histologically by noncaseating granulomas consisting of aggre…
pearls: Sarcoidosis is an inflammatory disorder characterized histologically by noncaseating granulomas consisting of aggregates of epithelioid macrophages and multinucleated giant cells.
Sarcoidosis is a noncaseating granulomatous disease that often involves the hilar lymph nodes and/or lungs. Risk factors include being female and African- American ethnicity.
Idiopathic autoimmune disorder that is one of the highest yield conditions on USMLE. You must know this condition extremely well.

topics.title: Mesothelioma

pearls: Malignant mesothelioma is a rare neoplasm typically arising from the pleura. It is strongly associated with asbestos exposure and presents with progressive dyspnea, cough, and chest pain.

In early mesothelioma, multiple nodules form on the parietal pleura and gradually encase the lung parenchyma Immunohistochemistry is important for diagnosis; nearly all mesotheliomas stain positive for cytokeratins and many also…
Cancer of “mesothelial cells” (answer on NBME) seen in patients with prior occupational exposure to asbestos.

topics.summary: Asbestos-related pleural disease is characterized by pleural plaques (focal pleural thickening, typically with calc…
pearls: Asbestos-related pleural disease is characterized by pleural plaques (focal pleural thickening, typically with calcifications).
This elderly patient had pleural plaques (focal thickening and calcification of the parietal pleura) and lower lung fibrosis, consistent with pleuropulmonary asbestosis.

topics.title: Silicosis
topics.summary: Silicosis is characterized by dyspnea and productive cough occurring years after inhalational exposure to crystalli…
pearls: Silicosis is characterized by dyspnea and productive cough occurring years after inhalational exposure to crystalline silica.

In silicosis, internalized silica particles impair macrophage function by disrupting phagocytosis and promoting apoptosis. This increases the risk of mycobacteria infection (particularly M tuberculosis).
Occupational exposure to silicon (sand) in foundry or stone quarry workers.

topics.title: Acute respiratory distress syndrome

pearls: Acute respiratory distress syndrome is a severe inflammatory reaction that occurs in the lungs and results in hypoxemia and noncardiogenic pulmonary edema.

The answer on USMLE for bilateral exudative chest infiltrates and ↓ O2 sats in patient following: pancreatitis; aspiration of vomitus; near-drowning episodes (aspiration of fresh/sea water); improper insertion of NG tube into the…

pearls: Acute pulmonary edema is a common consequence of acute myocardial infarction affecting the left ventricle.

pearls: Obstructive sleep apnea is characterized by sleep-related apnea/choking spells, loud snoring, disrupted sleep, excessive daytime somnolence, and symptoms that may overlap with depression (eg, low mood, fatigue, impaired…

pearls: Bosentan is a competitive antagonist of endothelin receptors used for the treatment of PAH.

pearls: This patient has hypertrophic osteoarthropathy (HOA), a syndrome characterized by painful bone and soft tissue enlargement in the distal extremities.

Radiation pneumonitis is a potential sequela of radiotherapy for the treatment of malignancy.

Fluid in the pleural space; often refers to “hydrothorax,” which means transudate or exudate of plasma-like fluid.

pearls: Parapneumonic effusions result from an inflammatory increase in vascular membrane permeability and therefore are exudative by Light criteria, which is confirmed by this patient's pleural fluid/serum lactate dehydrogenase ratio…
Empyema is an accumulation of pus within the pleural space that can result from multiple sources of bacterial contamination.

topics.summary: Primary spontaneous pneumothorax occurs in patients without preexisting pulmonary disease when a large change in th…
pearls: Primary spontaneous pneumothorax occurs in patients without preexisting pulmonary disease when a large change in the alveolar or intrapleural pressure results in a break in the visceral (eg, ruptured superficial bleb) pleura and…
Traumatic pneumothorax can involve puncture of either the chest wall (eg, penetrating chest trauma) or the lung (eg, by fractured ribs), allowing air to enter the pleural space.

Air in the pleural space. The terms almost always refers to a “spontaneous pneumothorax,” which will be acute-onset sharp chest pain in a tall, lanky patient in teens or 20s due to “ruptured subapical bleb.”

topics.title: Pneumonia
topics.summary: Lobar pneumonia is marked by the cytokine-mediated accumulation of neutrophils and proteinaceous material in the al…
pearls: Lobar pneumonia is marked by the cytokine-mediated accumulation of neutrophils and proteinaceous material in the alveoli.
Alveolar consolidation occurs when the alveoli become filled with fluid (eg, inflammatory exudate in bacterial pneumonia).
Lobar pneumonia = Strep pneumoniae on USMLE (right lower lobe consolidation with dullness to percussion).

topics.title: Lung abscess

pearls: Lung abscess is a necrotic infection of the pulmonary parenchyma that usually presents with several days of fever, cough productive of copious sputum (often foul-smelling), and chest x-ray evidence of cavitation with air-fluid…
Patients with alcohol use disorder are at increased risk for lung abscess due to the aspiration of oral flora during periods of unconsciousness.

topics.title: Lung cancer
topics.summary: Radon is a radioactive gas found throughout the earth that enters homes through contaminated soil and groundwater. …
pearls: Radon is a radioactive gas found throughout the earth that enters homes through contaminated soil and groundwater. It emits highly ionizing alpha radiation, causing DNA damage in the respiratory tract epithelium when inhaled.

Hamartomas are common, slow-growing, benign lung neoplasms microscopically characterized by nodules of disorganized, mature connective tissue (eg, cartilage, fat) and entrapped respiratory epithelium.

topics.title: Adenocarcinoma
topics.summary: Adenocarcinoma is the most common primary lung cancer in the general population, women, and nonsmokers. Epidermal g…
pearls: Adenocarcinoma is the most common primary lung cancer in the general population, women, and nonsmokers.

Adenocarcinoma, the most common pulmonary malignancy, is characterized histopathologically by invasive glandular cells with abundant cytoplasm and eccentrically placed nuclei; mucin production is common.
Adenocarcinoma means cancer of glands. If the Q says something about biopsy showing glandular morphology, you know they’re talking about adenocarcinoma.

pearls: This patient with an extensive smoking history who now has hemoptysis and shoulder pain likely has lung cancer, which can be associated with symptoms due to local or distant spread.

pearls: Extrinsic compression of the superior vena cava by a mediastinal mass (eg, malignancy) can cause superior vena cava syndrome, with impaired venous return from the upper body.

The intercostal and internal mammary veins provide an alternate route for blood from the upper extremities and head and neck to return to the inferior vena cava in the setting of a superior vena cava (SVC) obstruction.

topics.title: Brachiocephalic vein obstruction
topics.summary: The brachiocephalic vein drains the ipsilateral jugular and subclavian veins. The bilateral brachiocephalic veins c…
pearls: The brachiocephalic vein drains the ipsilateral jugular and subclavian veins. The bilateral brachiocephalic veins combine to form the superior vena cava (SVC).

pearls: First-generation antihistamines can cause significant side effects due to blockade of cholinergic, alpha-adrenergic, and serotonergic pathways. They should be avoided in older patients with cognitive or functional impairments.

pearls: Dextromethorphan (DXM) is a popular over-the-counter antitussive agent that acts on sigma receptors to suppress the medullary cough center. DXM also has an off-target action on serotonin transports and receptors in the CNS.

pearls: Topical preparations of α-adrenergic agonists cause vasoconstriction of the nasal mucosa vessels and are used as decongestants.

pearls: Simple squamous; flat and long in appearance; carries out gas exchange; 95% surface area of the alveoli.

Emphysema is destruction of alveolar surface area (i.e., mostly destruction of type I pneumocytes) → ↓ surface area for gas exchange → chronic CO2 retention → chronic respiratory acidosis (high bicarb to compensate).

pearls: Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 second.

↑ V/Q = reduced perfusion relative to ventilation.

pearls: As already mentioned above in the mesothelioma section, this is associated with shipyard workers, construction workers, and electricians. It can give rise to mesothelioma later in life.
The above ferruginous body is dumbbell-shape. Choose macrophage as the answer on USMLE for the cell that initiates pulmonary fibrosis (in response to asbestos and in general).
Causes restrictive lung pattern.

topics.title: General lung conditions

pearls: HY DDx on USMLE for a patient over the age of 50 who has 6-12+ months of unexplained dry cough. This is how it shows up 4/5 times.
Textbook restrictive lung disease, with ↔ or ↑ FEV1/FVC. The reason for the FEV1/FVC being greater than in obstructive lung disease is radial traction, as mentioned earlier.

CXR and CT scan show “reticular” or “reticulonodular” pattern. These descriptors are exceedingly HY on USMLE, where students will overlook them in the vignette, but they are hugely buzzy for restrictive lung disease.

pearls: Idiopathic autoimmune disease characterized by multi-organ system fibrosis and hardening of tissues (i.e., sclerosis).
Divided into limited and diffuse subtypes.
Limited scleroderma = CREST syndrome (Calcinosis, Raynaud’s, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasias). Associated with anti-centromere antibodies.

pearls: Difficult diagnosis on USMLE forms.
Diagnosis of exclusion, meaning all of these Qs require eliminating the other answer choices to get there.

The Q will say patient was in an accident + now has some form of difficulty breathing and patchy infiltrates in one or more areas of lung. They may or may not mention rib fractures just above the areas of infiltrates.

During embryologic development, several primitive renal structures form: the pronephros, mesonephros, and metanephros.

pearls: Extrinsic fetal compression from a low amniotic fluid level leads to Potter sequence with characteristic findings of flattened facies, limb deformities, and pulmonary hypoplasia.
Potter sequence results from a urinary tract anomaly (eg, bilateral renal agenesis) that causes decreased fetal urine output and severe oligohydramnios.

topics.summary: Horseshoe kidney is a congenital anomaly in which fusion of the metanephros (specifically, metanephric blastema) re…
pearls: Horseshoe kidney is a congenital anomaly in which fusion of the metanephros (specifically, metanephric blastema) results in fused renal parenchyma along the inferior poles.
Most patients remain asymptomatic but are at increased risk for recurrent nephroliths and urinary tract infections due to the abnormal orientation and positioning of the kidney.

topics.summary: Bladder outlet obstruction leads to increased pressure proximally and findings of bladder distension and wall thick…
pearls: Bladder outlet obstruction leads to increased pressure proximally and findings of bladder distension and wall thickening, secondary vesicoureteral reflux, ureteral dilation, and hydronephrosis.
Most common genitourinary abnormality in neonatal males.
Urethra has abnormal presence of valves at the posterior (prostatic) urethra, preventing the outflow of urine.

pearls: Vesicoureteral reflux typically occurs due to a congenitally shortened intravesical ureter length, which prevents complete closure of the ureterovesical junction and allows retrograde urine flow into the ureter during…
The kidney’s relatively low metabolic demands compared with high blood flow results in a small difference in renal arterial and venous Po2.
Congenital abnormality in which urine from the bladder can go back up into the ureter toward the kidney.

pearls: The ureters pass posterior to the ovarian (gonadal) vessels within the retroperitoneum and cross anterior to the common/external iliac arteries to reach the true pelvis.
To access the renal arteries from the femoral artery approach, the catheter should be advanced to the area just superior to the takeoff of the testicular artery.

topics.title: Fluid compartments

pearls: Total blood volume can be calculated by the following equation: Plasma volume (L) = Total Blood Volume (L) x (100% - hematocrit).

In this example, the patient’s plasma volume is three liters, Hematocrit is 40%. Therefore, 3L = Total Blood Volume x (100% - 40%) = Total Blood Volume x 60%. Dividing 3L by 60% solves for the Total Blood Volume, which is 5L.

topics.title: GFR
topics.summary: Glomerular filtration rate (GFR) can be assessed using an ideal filtration marker that is freely filtered across th…
pearls: Glomerular filtration rate (GFR) can be assessed using an ideal filtration marker that is freely filtered across the glomerulus and is not metabolized, secreted, or reabsorbed by the kidney tubules.
When the glomerular filtration rate (GFR) is normal, relatively large decreases in GFR result in only small increases in serum creatinine.

topics.title: Net filtration pressure
topics.summary: The net filtration pressure is a result of pressure gradients formed by Starling forces and is calculated by subtra…
pearls: The net filtration pressure is a result of pressure gradients formed by Starling forces and is calculated by subtracting the oncotic pressure gradient from the hydrostatic pressure gradient.

topics.summary: Constriction of the efferent (outgoing) arteriole will impede blood flow through the kidney. This will decrease RPF…
pearls: Constriction of the efferent (outgoing) arteriole will impede blood flow through the kidney.
Acute ureteral obstruction increases hydrostatic pressure proximal to the constriction. This pressure rise is transmitted back to the Bowman's space, resulting in decreased GFR.

topics.title: Aging
topics.summary: Normal aging results in multiple physiologic and structural alterations that lead to a slow decline in renal functi…
pearls: Normal aging results in multiple physiologic and structural alterations that lead to a slow decline in renal function.

The concentrating ability of the nephron in response to ADH decreases with time, which is reflected as a lower urine osmolality in older men as compared to younger men in the setting of water deprivation.

topics.title: Glucose clearance
topics.summary: At normal plasma concentrations of glucose, the renal tubules reabsorb the entire filtered load of glucose because …
pearls: At normal plasma concentrations of glucose, the renal tubules reabsorb the entire filtered load of glucose because it is below the maximum tubular reabsorption ability (transport maximum of glucose).

topics.title: Nephron transport physiology
topics.summary: Glucose is reabsorbed from the proximal tubule by sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT-2). Normally, nearly all fil…
pearls: Glucose is reabsorbed from the proximal tubule by sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT-2). Normally, nearly all filtered glucose is reabsorbed.
Regardless of the patient's hydration status, the majority of water reabsorption in the nephron occurs in the proximal tubule passively with the reabsorption of solutes.

topics.title: Antidiuretic hormone
topics.summary: Antidiuretic hormone acts on the medullary segment of the collecting duct to increase urea and water reabsorption, …
pearls: Antidiuretic hormone acts on the medullary segment of the collecting duct to increase urea and water reabsorption, allowing for the production of maximally concentrated urine.

Although the cortical collecting duct is impermeable to urea, vasopressin activates urea transporters in the medullary collecting duct, increasing urea reabsorption and decreasing renal urea clearance.

topics.title: Diuretics
topics.summary: Mannitol increases plasma osmolality, leading to the flow of water down its concentration gradient from the intrace…
pearls: Mannitol increases plasma osmolality, leading to the flow of water down its concentration gradient from the intracellular space to the plasma, helping to reduce intracranial pressure.
In the brain, water redistribution from the tissues into the plasma helps reduce edema and intracranial pressure in the setting of cerebral edema.
Osmotic diuretic that ↑ osmolality of urine, thereby retaining free water within the PCT and descending limb of loop of Henle.

topics.title: Thiazide diuretics
topics.summary: Thiazide diuretics work by blocking Na+-Cl- symporters in the distal convoluted tubules, causing enhanced Na, Cl, a…
pearls: Thiazide diuretics work by blocking Na+-Cl- symporters in the distal convoluted tubules, causing enhanced Na, Cl, and water excretion.

Thiazide diuretics effectively increase renal calcium reabsorption. In patients with recurrent calcium nephrolithiasis, thiazide diuretics can help prevent stone formation by decreasing urine Ca2+ excretion.

topics.title: Fanconi syndrome
topics.summary: This patient's glycosuria with normal serum glucose in combination with normal anion gap metabolic acidosis, hypoka…
pearls: This patient's glycosuria with normal serum glucose in combination with normal anion gap metabolic acidosis, hypokalemia, and hypophosphatemia is highly suggestive of impaired proximal tubular reabsorption .
Loss of bicarbonate causes persistent acidosis.
Inability of the PCT to reabsorb “lots of stuff.”

pearls: This patient has elevated serum aldosterone, a known cause of hypertension, hypokalemia, and muscle weakness. Hyperaldosteronism can be divided into primary and secondary etiologies.

Elevated serum aldosterone levels can manifest with hypertension, hypokalemia, and muscle weakness Increased levels of both renin and aldosterone are indicative of secondary hyperaldosteronism, which can be caused by renovascular…

pearls: The tubular fluid/plasma ultrafiltrate value (TF/P) The tubular fluid/plasma ultrafiltrate value is calculated by dividing the tubular fluid concentration of a given substance in the proximal tubule by the initial concentration…

Line 1 represents creatinine, which is freely filtered in the glomerulus, as well as actively secreted and not reabsorbed along the proximal tubule, resulting in a rapidly increasing concentration in the tubular fluid.

topics.title: ACE
topics.summary: Angiotensin I is then converted to angiotensin II, primarily within the small pulmonary vessels, by endothelial-bou…
pearls: Angiotensin I is then converted to angiotensin II, primarily within the small pulmonary vessels, by endothelial-bound angiotensin-converting enzyme.
Most angiotensin II is generated when angiotensin I passes through the pulmonary vascular endothelium, where ACE is highly expressed.
Carbonic anhydrase inhibitor (enzyme that enables H2CO3 ↔ HCO3- + H+) that acts within the tubular cells of the PCT.

topics.title: Juxtaglomerular apparatus
topics.summary: Renal artery stenosis causing significant renal hypoperfusion will result in a decreased glomerular filtration rate…
pearls: Renal artery stenosis causing significant renal hypoperfusion will result in a decreased glomerular filtration rate and activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system.
Beta-adrenergic blocking drugs inhibit renin release by blocking beta-1 receptor-mediated regulation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system.

topics.title: Angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors
topics.summary: Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors block the effect of ACE, decreasing angiotensin II and aldosterone l…
pearls: Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors block the effect of ACE, decreasing angiotensin II and aldosterone levels.
Common side-effects of ACE-inhibitors include decreased glomerular filtration rate (GFR), hyperkalemia, and cough. Angioedema is a rare, but life-threatening, side-effect.

topics.title: Angiotensin II receptor blockers (ARBs)
topics.summary: Angiotensin II receptor blockers (ARBs) work by blocking angiotensin II type 1 receptors, inhibiting the effects of…
pearls: Angiotensin II receptor blockers (ARBs) work by blocking angiotensin II type 1 receptors, inhibiting the effects of angiotensin II. This results in arterial vasodilation and decreased aldosterone secretion.
Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) reduce the risk of chronic kidney disease in patients with hypertension and diabetes.

topics.title: Aliskiren
topics.summary: direct renin inhibitor (eg, aliskiren) and ACE inhibitors decrease the effects of aldosterone by lowering circulati…
pearls: direct renin inhibitor (eg, aliskiren) and ACE inhibitors decrease the effects of aldosterone by lowering circulating levels of angiotensin II.
The renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) is integrally involved in the pathophysiology and treatment of hypertension.

topics.title: Erythropoietin (EPO)
topics.summary: Patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) often develop symptomatic anemia (eg, fatigue, exertional dyspnea) as th…
pearls: Patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) often develop symptomatic anemia (eg, fatigue, exertional dyspnea) as the glomerular filtration rate declines.

Patients with chronic kidney disease often develop normocytic anemia due to erythropoietin (EPO) deficiency. Treatment with recombinant EPO can dramatically improve tissue oxygen delivery and reduce mortality.

topics.title: Potassium shifts
topics.summary: Potassium is primarily stored intracellularly (~98% of total body stores) through the action of the Na-K-ATPase pum…
pearls: Potassium is primarily stored intracellularly (~98% of total body stores) through the action of the Na-K-ATPase pump.
This patient with a cocaine-induced myocardial infarction most likely developed acute hypokalemia due to stress-related beta-adrenergic hyperactivity, which causes potassium to shift intracellularly.
Will always be elevated in renal failure on USMLE.

topics.title: Acidosis and alkalosis
topics.summary: The kidneys can normally compensate somewhat for metabolic acidosis by completely reabsorbing filtered bicarbonate …
pearls: The kidneys can normally compensate somewhat for metabolic acidosis by completely reabsorbing filtered bicarbonate (HCO3-) and excreting excess H+ in the urine.

Acidosis stimulates renal ammoniagenesis, a process by which renal tubular epithelial cells metabolize glutamine to glutamate, generating ammonium that is excreted in the urine and bicarbonate that is absorbed into the blood.

topics.title: Respiratory acidosis
topics.summary: Respiratory acidosis presents with low pH and high PaCO2. HCO3− initially remains near normal but becomes elevated …
pearls: Respiratory acidosis presents with low pH and high PaCO2. HCO3− initially remains near normal but becomes elevated over several days as renal compensation develops.

Acute opioid overdose is characterized by altered level of consciousness, pinpoint pupils, and central respiratory depression. Patients are expected to have acute respiratory acidosis (low pH, high PaCO2) due to hypoventilation.

topics.title: Renal tubular acidosis
topics.summary: This patient has low serum bicarbonate (HCO3−) (<24 mEq/L), consistent with metabolic acidosis. The anion gap is no…
pearls: This patient has low serum bicarbonate (HCO3−) (<24 mEq/L), consistent with metabolic acidosis.
NAGMA results from loss of HCO3− (usually from the kidneys or gastrointestinal tract), leading to a relative increase in H+.

pearls: Poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis is the most common cause of nephritic syndrome (eg, hematuria, edema, hypertension) in children, typically occuring 2-4 weeks after a streptococcal infection (eg, impetigo, cellulitis…

pearls: IgA nephropathy is characterized as recurrent hematuria that occurs spontaneously or within a few days of upper respiratory or pharyngeal infection (synpharyngitic hematuria).

Aka Berger disease; IgA deposition in renal mesangium.

topics.title: Rapidly progressive (crescentic) glomerulonephritis (RPGN)

pearls: Crescent formation on light microscopy is diagnostic of rapidly progressive (crescentic) glomerulonephritis (RPGN).

pearls: Membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis is typically caused by immune complex deposition within the glomerular capillary walls and mesangium and can be associated with chronic infections (eg, hepatitis B).
This patient's acute kidney injury (eg, elevated creatinine), proteinuria, hypertension, and glomerular hematuria (eg, red cell casts) are indicative of glomerulonephritis (GN).

topics.title: Nephrotic syndrome

pearls: Frothy or foamy urine may be caused by proteinuria. Heavy proteinuria, as in nephrotic syndrome, can cause regional or generalized interstitial edema because the decrease in serum albumin and total protein concentrations lowers…
This child most likely has minimal change disease, the most common cause of nephrotic syndrome in children. It typically presents suddenly after an upper respiratory infection.
Nephritic conditions have blood in the urine; nephrotic syndromes don’t.

pearls: This patient with weight gain and edema with 4+ protein and oval fat bodies on urinalysis has nephrotic syndrome. The presence of phospholipase A2 receptor (PLA2R) antibodies suggests a diagnosis of membranous nephropathy.

Membranous nephropathy is the most common nephrotic syndrome in Caucasian adults and can be primary (idiopathic) or secondary to conditions such as systemic lupus erythematosus, autoimmune disease against phospholipase…

topics.summary: This patient has type 2 diabetes mellitus, confirmed by elevated blood glucose and hemoglobin A1c. One of the earli…
pearls: This patient has type 2 diabetes mellitus, confirmed by elevated blood glucose and hemoglobin A1c.

topics.title: Kidney stones
topics.summary: Urine sediment in acute ureterolithiasis typically shows free red blood cells (hematuria) and crystals consistent w…
pearls: Urine sediment in acute ureterolithiasis typically shows free red blood cells (hematuria) and crystals consistent with the type of stone.
Urine supersaturation is the main mechanism underlying all types of renal stones. Low fluid intake increases the concentration of stone-forming agents, thereby promoting stone formation.

topics.summary: Formation of uric acid kidney stones is promoted by low urine pH, which favors formation of insoluble uric acid ove…
pearls: Formation of uric acid kidney stones is promoted by low urine pH, which favors formation of insoluble uric acid over soluble urate ion.
Dd> Overproduction of uric acid (eg, gout, myeloproliferative disorders) can lead to uric acid stones.
Seen in patients who have gout. Not complicated.

pearls: Benign prostatic hyperplasia leads to progressive bladder outlet obstruction. Over time, increased urinary pressures can cause hydronephrosis and renal parenchymal atrophy with scarring.
Fibrosis and strictures are late effects of radiation therapy. Radiotherapy for prostate cancer may lead to urethral fibrosis and result in obstructive uropathy.

topics.summary: Stress urinary incontinence is involuntary urine leakage with increased intraabdominal pressure (eg, coughing, snee…
pearls: Stress urinary incontinence is involuntary urine leakage with increased intraabdominal pressure (eg, coughing, sneezing).
Stress incontinence, involuntary leakage of urine with increased intraabdominal pressure, can occur due to urethral sphincter dysfunction (eg, decreased sphincter tone).

topics.summary: This patient's findings suggest overflow incontinence, which is mainly due to impaired detrusor contractility or bl…
pearls: This patient's findings suggest overflow incontinence, which is mainly due to impaired detrusor contractility or bladder outlet obstruction (eg, tumor obstructing the urethra).

Pelvic parasympathetic nerves in the pelvic nerve plexus function to excite and contract the bladder via muscarinic acetylcholine receptors while sympathetic nerves mediate relaxation of the internal urethral sphincter via…
