vignettes.q: 34F + left eye pain + blurry vision + progressive weakness of right arm and both legs + fundoscopy shows optic disc swelling + MRI shows multiple T2-weighted bright signal abnormalities in white matter; what ce
vignettes.a: oligodendrocytes; Dx is multiple Sclerosis; mechanism is T cell-mediated destruction of oligodendrocytes in CNS (in contrast, Schwann cell destruction in PNS is Guillain-Barre); oligodendrocytes synthesize myelin in the CNS; Schwa

vignettes.q: 81M + stroke + which type of cell of CNS is likely to clear necrotic tissue in the affected area?
vignettes.a: microglial cells (macrophages of the CNS).

vignettes.q: What cell does HIV infect in the CNS?
vignettes.a: microglia; microglia in the CNS are one of the major cellular reservoirs of HIV.

vignettes.q: 44M + long Hx of alcoholism + stumbles to the right when ambulating + Romberg sign intact; where is the location of his pathology?
vignettes.a: right side of cerebellum; cerebellar lesions always ipsilateral; lateral aspects of cerebellum result in ipsilateral limb ataxia; midline cerebellar lesions (vermis) result in truncal ataxia; Romberg sign is (+) if etiology for at

vignettes.q: 51F + irregular flailing movements of right side of body; Dx and site of lesion?
vignettes.a: hemiballismus; lesion of contralateral (left) subthalamic nucleus.

vignettes.q: 7M + ingested substance under the kitchen since + vomiting; what part of the brain is most likely responsible for the vomiting, and where is it located?
vignettes.a: area postrema, which is a chemotactic trigger zone for emesis; it is located on the dorsal aspect of the medulla at the caudal 4th ventricle.

vignettes.q: 51M + hereditary hemochromatosis + isolated decrease in serum gonadotropins; where is the most likely location of the pathology?
vignettes.a: hypothalamus → iron deposition in hypothalamus resulting in decreased GnRH; if deposition were in anterior pituitary, then we’d likely get a decrease in the other anterior pituitary hormones as well, rather than an isolated decrea

vignettes.q: What are the hormones secreted by the anterior pituitary?
vignettes.a: LH, FSH, TSH, ACTH, GH, prolactin.

vignettes.q: What are the hormones stored by the posterior pituitary?
vignettes.a: vasopressin (ADH), oxytocin; these hormones are not synthesized in the posterior pituitary; they are synthesized in the hypothalamus and then merely stored in the posterior pituitary.

vignettes.q: What are the hormones secreted by the hypothalamus that regulate the anterior pituitary hormones?
vignettes.a: GnRH (stimulates LH, FSH); TRH (stimulates TSH); CRH (stimulates ACTH); GHRH (stimulates GH); dopamine (inhibits prolactin).

vignettes.q: 16F + MVA + pituitary stalk is severed; which hormone will increase?
vignettes.a: prolactin; all hypothalamic hormones are stimulatory except for dopamine’s actions on prolactin, which are inhibitory.

vignettes.q: 54F + decreased fluency of spontaneous speech after a cerebral infarction + comprehension is normal + examination shows weakness of lower 2/3 of right side of face; Dx? + which vessel did the stroke occur?
vignettes.a: Broca aphasia; left middle cerebral artery.

vignettes.q: 65M + BP 140/100 + 2/5 muscle strength in left leg + brisk reflexes in left leg; which vessel is the most likely site of the stroke?
vignettes.a: right anterior cerebral artery.

vignettes.q: 24F + complains that food has lost its flavor ever since she got hit in the head during a softball game last week; damage to which structure may have occurred?
vignettes.a: cribriform plate; olfactory nerve lesion leads to decreased perception of taste.

vignettes.q: 81F + difficulty fastening buttons + weakness of intrinsic muscles of hands + loss of sensation in 5th fingers; Q asks for Dx at level of spine
vignettes.a: C7-T1 foraminal stenosis.

vignettes.q: 34F + Hx of MS + two-week Hx of severe shooting pain in left cheek brought on by brushing teeth; what is the most likely location of the demyelination leading to this patient’s presentation?
vignettes.a: pons (giving rise to trigeminal nerve; in this case MS patient with trigeminal neuralgia-like presentation from central lesion).

vignettes.q: 61F + brought to ER by police after she was wandering around the city confused + disheveled + broad- based gait and nystagmus + results of alcohol and drug screening are negative; brain MRI will show atrophy of
vignettes.a: mammillary bodies; Dx is Wernicke encephalopathy (ACOW → Ataxia, Confusion, Ophthalmoplegia, Wernicke encephalopathy).

vignettes.q: 55M + two-week Hx of constant and intense pain of left arm + Hx of stroke 5 months ago resulting in loss of sensation to left side of body + examination shows decreased light touch, vibration, pain, and tempera
vignettes.a: right thalamus; thalamic pain syndrome is a HY post-stroke cause of pain.

vignettes.q: 42F + struck in left eye by a golf ball + presents with diplopia, periorbital swelling, and enophthalmos + upward gaze is impaired + sensation is decreased over the left zygoma + x-ray shows orbital floor fract
vignettes.a: inferior rectus and inferior oblique.

vignettes.q: 77M + sudden-onset miosis of left eye + ptosis of left eyelid + dysphagia + difficulty speaking + pain and Temperature are decreased on left side of her face and right side of body; which artery is most likely
vignettes.a: left posterior inferior cerebellar artery; Horner syndrome as associated with PICA infarct (lateral medullary syndrome) is HY.

vignettes.q: 15M + pain and tingling in her right hand when she goes backpacking + symptoms resolve five minutes after she takes her backpack off; Dx?
vignettes.a: thoracic outlet syndrome due to first cervical rib.

vignettes.q: 26F + tonic-clonic seizure + immediately prior smelled foul odor for several seconds; where did the seizure most likely originate from?
vignettes.a: temporal lobe.

vignettes.q: 69M + stroke + hoarse voice + can't detect pinprick or cold on right side of face or left side of body; what’s the location of the stroke?
vignettes.a: lateral medulla (right PICA); once again, lateral medullary syndrome = PICAchew (Pikachu) → dysphagia/hoarseness +/- Horner syndrome.

vignettes.q: 18M + used “synthetic heroine” at party + tight muscles + shuffling gait + bradykinesia + afebrile and pupils normal; Q asks location of the brain affected?
vignettes.a: substantia nigra; MPTP-induced Parkinsonism is assessed on both USMLE Step 1; MPTP is sold as “synthetic heroine” and can cause Parkinsonism.

vignettes.q: 28F + urinary incontinence + blurry vision + diminished vibration in the toes + unable to maintain balance with eyes closed; Q asks damage to which spinal tract?
vignettes.a: fasciculus gracilis of the dorsal columns; in contrast, fasciculus cuneatus would do vibration/proprioception of upper limbs; diagnosis here is MS presenting with classic urge incontinence, optic neuritis, and a (+) Romberg sign.

vignettes.q: 3M + moderate strabismus; if not treated, she'll have deficits in depth perception due to lack of appropriate competitive interactions in the visual cortex; calcium entry through which receptor mediates the out
vignettes.a: Answer = NMDA (glutamate) receptors; yes, weird, but handle it.

vignettes.q: Newborn + strabismus; what's the rationale for surgically correcting this problem during early childhood?
vignettes.a: if not, normal binocular vision won't develop.

vignettes.q: 23M + inferonasal “bleeding” of the pupil + incomplete closure of embryonic fissure of what structure in the right eye is most likely responsible?
vignettes.a: iris. Student says “?” → CHARGE syndrome presents with coloboma of the eye, where the iris fails to develop properly, resulting in a “bleeding” of the pupil.

vignettes.q: 57F + invasive gall bladder cancer + 3-week Hx of severe left-sided back and abdominal pain; an operation scheduled to relieve pain would target which spinal tract?
vignettes.a: right spinothalamic tract (contralateral).

vignettes.q: 22F + fluoxetine prescribed; benefit occurs due to effects on neurons located where?
vignettes.a: raphe nuclei (serotonin-secreting neurons).

vignettes.q: 42F + 4-month Hx of abnormal tingling that started in right hand has progressed to right arm and right side of face; cause of her Sx is a lesion located in which cerebral cortex gyri?
vignettes.a: left post- central (i.e., posterior to the central sulcus, which is where the primary sensory cortex is).

vignettes.q: 44M + progressive ataxia with unsteady gait + left-sided intention tremors; cause is damage to which brain area?
vignettes.a: left cerebellar hemisphere (cerebellar lesions lead to ipsilateral neurologic signs).

vignettes.q: 72F + loss of pain and temperature on left side of face and right of the body + paralysis of vocal cords on left + loss of gag reflex on left; what part of the brainstem is most likely affected?
vignettes.a: left dorsolateral medulla; lateral medullary syndrome; CN IX/V dysfunction; vocal cords are recurrent laryngeal nerves (of vagus); gag reflex is CN IX afferent and CN X efferent.

vignettes.q: 54F + 4-day Hx of hoarseness and difficulty swallowing + unable to elevate left side of palate; which CN is damaged?
vignettes.a: left vagus nerve; failure of elevation of ipsilateral palate causes contralateral uvula deviation.

vignettes.q: 54M + Hx of HTN + unable to recognize people’s face + unable to recognize objects unless he touches them or hears sounds they make; damaged area of brain is supplied by what artery?
vignettes.a: posterior cerebral artery; prosopagnosia (inability to recognize faces) and visual agnosia (inability to recognize objects upon seeing them) are associated with occipital lobe lesions (PCA infarct).

vignettes.q: 61F + undergoes repair of leaking saccular aneurysm + postoperative CT scan shows widening of subarachnoid space; what changes in CSF are the most likely cause of these findings?
vignettes.a: decreased movement of CSF through the arachnoid villi.

vignettes.q: 24M + decreased taste to anterior 2/3 of left side of tongue; which nerve is likely damaged?
vignettes.a: left facial nerve.

vignettes.q: The thalamus notably does not receive sensory input from which nerve?
vignettes.a: olfactory nerve.

vignettes.q: Stroke affecting ventral posterolateral (VPL) & ventral posteromedial (VPM) nuclei of thalamus results in what kind of deficit?
vignettes.a: pure sensory; VPL senses from body; VPM from face.

vignettes.q: 59M + Parkinson disease; loss of patient’s substantia nigra is most likely to result in disinhibition in which brain area?
vignettes.a: striatum.

vignettes.q: 45M + uvula deviation to the right + dysphagia; which tongue muscle might be affected?
vignettes.a: palatoglossus (innervated by CN X); other tongue muscles innervated by CN XII.

vignettes.q: 29M + MVA + hematoma over mastoid processes bilaterally + rhinorrhea + otorrhea + raccoon eyes; Dx?
vignettes.a: base of skull fracture (classic tetrad).

vignettes.q: 31F + MVA + GCS of 6 + BP 165/90 + RR 10 + HR 55; what is the mechanism for this patient’s hypertension?
vignettes.a: increased intracranial pressure (Cushing triad of HTN, bradycardia, bradypnea).

vignettes.q: 59F + metastatic breast cancer + absent corneal reflex on right; metastases to which cranial nerve exit point might be responsible for this neuro exam finding?
vignettes.a: superior orbital fissure → exit point for ophthalmic branch of trigeminal nerve; V1 → Standing Room Only → Superior orbital fissure, foramen Rotundum, foramen Ovale; for V1, V2, V3, respectively.

vignettes.q: 24M + herpes encephalitis + treated with IV acyclovir + months later has hyperphagia, hypersexuality, hyperorality; Dx?
vignettes.a: Kluver-Bucy syndrome (bilateral amygdala lesions); KB syndrome can be a rare complication of HSV encephalitis.

vignettes.q: 71F + stroke + now has agraphia, acalculia, finger agnosia, and left-right agnosia; what part of the brain did the stroke occur?
vignettes.a: angular gyrus (parietal lobe); Dx = Gerstmann syndrome.

vignettes.q: 23M + near-drowning episode with hypoxia to brain; what change might be seen in the hippocampi of this patient?
vignettes.a: “red neurons” → pathologic staining pattern of neurons during acute hypoxic injury; hippocampi notably susceptible to ischemia → results in anterograde amnesia.

vignettes.q: 40F + episodes of feeling like the room is spinning + sometimes associated with vomiting + physician is able to reproduce the Sx with the Dix-Hallpike maneuver; what is the mechanism for this patient’s conditio
vignettes.a: “posterior semicircular canal otolith”; Dx = benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV); Tx with Epley maneuver.

vignettes.q: 40F + viral infection + tinnitus + hearing loss + vertigo; Dx?
vignettes.a: labyrinthitis.

vignettes.q: 40F + viral infection + vertigo; Dx?
vignettes.a: vestibular neuritis.

vignettes.q: 31M + warm water instilled into left ear causes nystagmus, but warm water in right ear does not cause nystagmus; where is the site of the lesion? → right-sided vestibular apparatus.
vignettes.a: Called the vestibular caloric reflex test. Warm water instilled into ear causes endolymph on ipsilateral side to move, mimicking a head turn to the ipsilateral side. This causes eye movement to the contralateral side, with nystagm

vignettes.q: Shining light in either eyes causes direct and consensual pupillary constriction; this clinical maneuver is a test of functional integrity of what?
vignettes.a: midbrain (Edinger-Westphal nucleus).

vignettes.q: 24M + left eye fails to constrict when light is shone in both the left and right eyes; where is the lesion
vignettes.a: oculomotor nerve (CN III).

vignettes.q: 24M + light directed into right eye results in constriction of right pupil but not left pupil + light directed into patient's left eye results in constriction of right pupil but not left pupil; where is the sit
vignettes.a: left oculomotor nerve (CN III); same thing as prior Q, but worded differently.

vignettes.q: 69M + smoker for 50 years + constricted left pupil + left eyelid droopy + skin dry on left side of face; where is the lesion?
vignettes.a: Pancoast tumor of lung resulting in impingement on superior cervical ganglia (Horner syndrome).

vignettes.q: 24M + burning vesicular lesions around the lips; Q asks about the mechanism of this pathogen’s presentation
vignettes.a: NBME answer = “reactivation in sensory neurons” → herpes labialis (HSV1/2) → virus lies dormant in trigeminal nerve (V2 – maxillary branch; V3 – mandibular branch).

vignettes.q: 3-day-old male + born at home + umbilical cord tied with twine + arching of back; mechanism for disease process?
vignettes.a: “blockade of inhibitory neurotransmitter release” → tetanus toxin causes decreased presynaptic release of GABA and glycine by inhibiting SNARE protein; USMLE might show you a drawing of where the toxin acts, and the answer is insi

vignettes.q: Diarrhea + Guillain-Barre syndrome
vignettes.a: Campylobacter

vignettes.q: Guillain-Barré syndrome CSF?
vignettes.a: albuminocytologic dissociation (high protein + normal cells)

vignettes.q: Guillain-Barré syndrome Dx?
vignettes.a: electromyography + nerve conduction studies (on NBME)

vignettes.q: Ataxia, confusion, ophthalmoplegia
vignettes.a: Wernicke encephalopathy (B1 deficiency)

vignettes.q: Retrograde amnesia + confabulation in alcoholic
vignettes.a: Korsakoff psychosis

vignettes.q: Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome
vignettes.a: mammillary bodies

vignettes.q: Incontinence in multiple sclerosis patient or perimenopausal
vignettes.a: urge incontinence

vignettes.q: Gradual-onset dementia + no sensory or motor dysfunction
vignettes.a: Alzheimer

vignettes.q: Mini-mental state exam score low + patient tries to do well
vignettes.a: Alzheimer Mini-mental state exam score low + patient is apathetic / takes long to perform tasks / does poorly on reverse

vignettes.q: Patient complains about memory loss
vignettes.a: normal aging, not Alzheimer

vignettes.q: First-line Tx for Alzheimer
vignettes.a: donepezil (cholinesterase inhibitor → increases cholinergic transmission); can also give galantamine or rivastigmine

vignettes.q: NMDA receptor (glutamate receptor) antagonist used in Alzheimer Tx
vignettes.a: memantine

vignettes.q: Visual hallucinations + Parkinsonism + dementia
vignettes.a: Lewy body dementia

vignettes.q: Apathy + disinhibition + personality change + dementia
vignettes.a: frontotemporal dementia (Pick disease)

vignettes.q: Urinary incontinence + ataxia + CNS dysfunction (wet, wobbly, wacky)
vignettes.a: Normal-pressure hydrocephalus

vignettes.q: Wet, wobbly, wacky + Parkinsonism
vignettes.a: still NPH

vignettes.q: Parkinsonism in older patient
vignettes.a: Parkinson disease

vignettes.q: Parkinsonism + axial dystonia
vignettes.a: progressive supranuclear palsy

vignettes.q: Viral infection + tinnitus + vertigo +/- neurosensory hearing loss
vignettes.a: labrynthitis

vignettes.q: Tx for multiple sclerosis flares
vignettes.a: IV steroids (IV methylprednisolone)

vignettes.q: Given to MS patients between flares
vignettes.a: interferon-beta

vignettes.q: Incontinence in MS
vignettes.a: urge (hyperactive detrusor, as mentioned earlier)

vignettes.q: Hematuria + hemoptysis + “head-itis” (mastoiditis, sinusitis, otitis, nasal septal perforation)
vignettes.a: Wegener

vignettes.q: Tx of tinea pedis
vignettes.a: topical terbinafine or topical azole

vignettes.q: Tx of tinea corporis (ring worm)
vignettes.a: topical azole (clotrimazole or miconazole)

vignettes.q: Tx of tinea versicolor
vignettes.a: topical selenium

vignettes.q: Most common cause of otitis media
vignettes.a: Strep pneumo

vignettes.q: Tx of otitis media
vignettes.a: oral amoxicillin only

vignettes.q: Tx of recurrent OM
vignettes.a: amoxicillin/clavulanate

vignettes.q: When to do tympanostomy tube
vignettes.a: three or more OM in 6 months, or 4 or more in a year

vignettes.q: Tx of otitis externa
vignettes.a: topical ciprofloxacin + hydrocortisone drops

vignettes.q: High BP + smoker + TIA or stroke or retinal artery occlusion. How to best decrease stroke risk
vignettes.a: lisinopril, not smoking cessation

vignettes.q: Hypertensive pt + stroke
vignettes.a: do carotid duplex ultrasound

vignettes.q: Normotensive pt + stroke
vignettes.a: do ECG; if ECG normal → Holter monitor

vignettes.q: Prophylaxis for otitis externa (i.e., in someone with continued water exposure, like crew)
vignettes.a: topical alcohol-acetic acid drops

vignettes.q: Otitis externa + mastoiditis
vignettes.a: malignant otitis externa

vignettes.q: Tx of otitis media
vignettes.a: amoxicillin (amoxicillin/clavulanate [Augmentin] is the wrong answer initially; use Augmentin for recurrent OM)

vignettes.q: When to do a tympanostomy tube?
vignettes.a: 3+ OM in a 6-month period or 4+ in a year

vignettes.q: When do you do CT head before LP in suspected meningitis?
vignettes.a: Confusion that interferes with neurologic exam / decreased GCS score Seizure Focal neurologic signs (motor or sensory) Papilledema or if the optic fundi cannot be visualized Above reasons indicate potential mass lesion, where if y

vignettes.q: Is tPA ever an answer for anything?
vignettes.a: Ischemic stroke within 4.5 hours. Must do non-contrast CT of the head to confirm no bleed before giving tPA.

vignettes.q: 72M has 30 minutes of facial drooping + arm weakness since waking up from a nap
vignettes.a: amount of time since stroke = amount of time that has passed since he was last known to be normal (i.e., before he went to sleep) → on the USMLE, this situation often means don’t give the tPA.

vignettes.q: Urge incontinence
vignettes.a: “hyperactive detrusor,” or “detrusor instability” → needs to run to the bathroom when sticking a key in the front door; needs to run to bathroom when opening car door; answer in multiple sclerosis + menopause (part of vasomotor Sx

vignettes.q: Woman who works in dental care with vesicle on finger; Dx?
vignettes.a: herpetic whitlow → HSV1/2 of the finger → treat with oral acyclovir (in real life will give both oral and topical; on the USMLE, answer is always oral)

vignettes.q: 14M + ataxia + cognitive decline over a few months
vignettes.a: glue, not alcohol → no way a kid that young would get alcoholic cerebellar ataxia; this is on the NBME even if you find it stupid/weird.

vignettes.q: Tx for spasticity in MS
vignettes.a: baclofen.

vignettes.q: Dx of MS
vignettes.a: choose MRI over CSF IgG oligoclonal bands if both are listed.

vignettes.q: Urinary incontinence in MS
vignettes.a: urge incontinence (hyperactive detrusor / detrusor instability)

vignettes.q: AV-nicking on fundoscopy
vignettes.a: hypertensive retinopathy

vignettes.q: 72M + drooping of left side of face + decreased muscle strength and increased tendon reflexes of both left upper and lower extremities + Babinski on left + intact sensation; what’s the most likely explanation f
vignettes.a: lacunar infarct of internal capsule; produces “pure motor” stroke in most cases of posterior capsule infarct; thalamic stroke produces “pure sensory” effects; lacunar infarcts are usually due to Hx of HTN causes lipohyalinosis of

vignettes.q: 40F undergoing chemotherapy + has low leukocyte count; what drug will help this patient?
vignettes.a: pegfilgrastim (granulocyte colony-stimulating factor; G-CSF); will cause an increase in neutrophils.

vignettes.q: 25M + 3-day Hx of paresthesias of the legs + difficulty swallowing + diminished tendon reflexes + CSF shows protein of 70 mg/dL and cell count of 5/uL; what’s the mechanism for this patient’s condition?
vignettes.a: “destruction of myelin and endoneurial lymphocytic infiltrates”; USMLE wants you to know this description of Guillain-Barre; CSF findings are albuminocytologic dissociation (increased protein but normal cells).

vignettes.q: 39M + bilateral renal enlargement + high blood pressure + father died from subarachnoid hemorrhage; this patient most likely has a gene mutation in which protein?
vignettes.a: polycystin; diagnosis is ADPKD; high blood pressure is from cysts impinging on the renal microvasculature leading to surges in RAAS.

vignettes.q: 50F + subarachnoid hemorrhage; Q asks biggest risk factor
vignettes.a: HTN most common overall in general population; otherwise, if patient has ADPKS or Ehlers-Danlos, those would be more specific.

vignettes.q: 82F + wobbly gait for 4 months + head CT shows crescent-shaped bleed; what is biggest risk factor?
vignettes.a: diagnosis is subdural hematoma; often slow-accumulating; elderly have reduced cerebral volume, making superior cerebral (bridging) veins more susceptible to friability; other notable risk factors are alcoholism, dementia (further

vignettes.q: 81M + Alzheimer + recurrent hemorrhagic stroke; what is major risk factor for the bleeds?
vignettes.a: Alzheimer → can lead to amyloid angiopathy, causing intracerebral/intraparenchymal hemorrhage that presents as recurrent hemorrhagic stroke.

vignettes.q: 25M + uses a variety of illicit drugs + develops Parkinsonism; risk factor?
vignettes.a: MPTP use (synthetic heroin) can cause Parkinsonism.

vignettes.q: 28F + eating clay, starch, and ice; Dx + risk factor?
vignettes.a: pica due to iron deficiency.

vignettes.q: 44M + ataxia + confusion + ophthalmoplegia + confabulations; what is risk factor for this condition
vignettes.a: alcoholism causing thiamine deficiency, resulting in Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome (WKS). ACOW → Ataxia, Confusion, Ophthalmoplegia = Wernicke. If we add confabulations (Korsakoff psychosis) on top of ACOW, we now call it WKS.

vignettes.q: 60F + lung cancer + difficulty getting up from chair a few times; Dx + risk factor?
vignettes.a: Lambert-Eaton due to small cell (anti-presynaptic voltage-gated Ca channel antibodies).

vignettes.q: 60F + lung cancer + ataxia; Dx + risk factor?
vignettes.a: small cell cerebellar dysfunction (anti-Hu/-Yo) Abs.

vignettes.q: 35F + worsening diplopia, dysphagia, and eyelid ptosis over the course of a day; Dx and risk factor?
vignettes.a: myasthenia gravis (Abs against post-synaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors); often idiopathic, but can be due to thymoma as risk factor.

vignettes.q: Low calcium or potassium not responsive to supplementation
vignettes.a: cause is low Mg

vignettes.q: Hx of many pregnancies + downward movement of vesicourethral junction
vignettes.a: stress incontinence

vignettes.q: Hyperactive detrusor or detrusor instability
vignettes.a: urge incontinence

vignettes.q: Need to run to bathroom when sticking key in a door
vignettes.a: urge incontinence

vignettes.q: Incontinence + high post-void volume (usually 3-400 in question; normal is <50 mL)
vignettes.a: overflow incontinence

vignettes.q: Incontinence in diabetes
vignettes.a: overflow incontinence due to neurogenic bladder

vignettes.q: Costovertebral angle tenderness + fever
vignettes.a: pyelonephritis

vignettes.q: Tx for pyelonephritis
vignettes.a: ciprofloxacin, OR ampicillin + gentamicin

vignettes.q: Saddle anesthesia + urinary retention
vignettes.a: cauda equina syndrome

vignettes.q: Perianal anesthesia + urinary retention or incontinence
vignettes.a: conus medullaris syndrome

vignettes.q: serial 7s
vignettes.a: depression (pseudodementia)

vignettes.q: Step-wise dementia/decline and/or sensory/motor disturbance
vignettes.a: vascular dementia

vignettes.q: Tx of UTI
vignettes.a: TMP/SMX or nitrofurantoin

vignettes.q: Tx of cystitis
vignettes.a: nitrofurantoin (need not be pregnant)

vignettes.q: Weakened biceps + loss of sensation of lateral forearm
vignettes.a: musculocutaneous nerve injury

vignettes.q: Paresthesias + pain following burn or casting
vignettes.a: compartment syndrome

vignettes.q: Compartment syndrome Dx
vignettes.a: measure compartment pressure

vignettes.q: Lumbosacral strain diagnosis
vignettes.a: DO NOT x-ray

vignettes.q: Lumbosacral strain Tx
vignettes.a: NSAIDs + exercise as tolerated; bedrest is the WRONG answer

vignettes.q: Point tenderness over a vertebra in IV drug user
vignettes.a: epidural abscess

vignettes.q: “Step-off” of one vertebra relative to another
vignettes.a: spondylolisthesis

vignettes.q: Dx of AS
vignettes.a: x-ray of sacroiliac joints

vignettes.q: Back pain worse when standing or walking for long periods of time
vignettes.a: lumbar spinal stenosis

vignettes.q: Back in pain in patient with history of other type of cancer
vignettes.a: metastases

vignettes.q: Suspected spinal mets
vignettes.a: MRI

vignettes.q: Pruritis after shower
vignettes.a: basophilia

vignettes.q: High hemoglobin + lung disease / low pO2
vignettes.a: secondary polycythemia (high EPO)

vignettes.q: Blurry vision or Raynaud or pain in fingers or headache
vignettes.a: hyperviscosity syndrome

vignettes.q: Fixed splitting of S2
vignettes.a: atrial septal defect

vignettes.q: Mid-systolic click
vignettes.a: MVP

vignettes.q: Screening at age 50
vignettes.a: mammogram (every two years) + colonoscopy (every ten years)

vignettes.q: Anuria (no urine output) after removal of catheter
vignettes.a: acute urethral obstruction

vignettes.q: Contrast induced nephropathy; how to prevent
vignettes.a: saline hydration beforehand

vignettes.q: Blood loss + obstetric catastrophe
vignettes.a: diffuse cortical necrosis

vignettes.q: 2+ blood in urine but 0-4 RBCs/HPF on LM
vignettes.a: false + blood on dipstick → myoglobinuria → rhabdomyolysis

vignettes.q: Preferred antibiotic in sepsis
vignettes.a: ceftriaxone

vignettes.q: Sepsis Tx in young children
vignettes.a: cefotaxime

vignettes.q: Tx for spontaneous bacterial peritonitis
vignettes.a: ceftriaxone

vignettes.q: SBP Dx
vignettes.a: paracentesis (peritoneal aspiration; don’t confuse with periocardiocentesis) + do gram-stain + look for >250 WBCs per HPF

vignettes.q: Diabetic gastroparesis before giving med
vignettes.a: endoscopy first to rule out physical obstruction

vignettes.q: Endoscopy negative for diabetic gastroparesis
vignettes.a: do gastric-emptying scintigraphy

vignettes.q: Pt doesn’t want surgery or is pregnant
vignettes.a: ursodeoxycholic acid (ursodiol)

vignettes.q: Hx of surgery + high-pitched bowel sounds or acute-onset abdo symptoms
vignettes.a: small bowel obstruction (SBO)

vignettes.q: Increased calcium in sarcoid
vignettes.a: means decreased calcium in feces (bc D3 increased small bowel absorption)

vignettes.q: Tx for sarcoid
vignettes.a: steroids

vignettes.q: New name for Wegener
vignettes.a: granulomatosis with polyangiitis

vignettes.q: Dx of Wegener
vignettes.a: c-ANCA (anti-PR3; anti-proteinase 3)

vignettes.q: New name for CS
vignettes.a: eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis

vignettes.q: Dx of CS
vignettes.a: p-ANCA (anti-MPO; anti-myeloperoxidase)

vignettes.q: Hematuria in isolation + p-ANCA in serum
vignettes.a: microscopic polyangiitis (MP)

vignettes.q: Dx and Tx of choledocholithiasis
vignettes.a: ERCP

vignettes.q: Recent cholecystectomy + fever + abdo pain
vignettes.a: post-op bile leak

vignettes.q: cyst
vignettes.a: do simple excision of cyst (cholangiocarcinoma not cystic + CT can be negative)

vignettes.q: Imaging to view liver or pancreas
vignettes.a: CT with contrast

vignettes.q: Imaging to view gallbladder
vignettes.a: Ultrasound

vignettes.q: Imaging to view bile ducts
vignettes.a: ERCP or MRCP (choose ERCP > MRCP if both listed)

vignettes.q: MCC
vignettes.a: T cell dysfunction = impaired cell-mediated immunity on the USMLE

vignettes.q: Hyper IgM syndrome
vignettes.a: deficiency of CD40 ligand on T cell (can’t activate CD40 on B cell to induce isotype class switching)

vignettes.q: Greasy, scaly scalp + itchy + papules + adult
vignettes.a: seborrheic dermatitis

vignettes.q: Tx for SD
vignettes.a: azole or selenium shampoo

vignettes.q: Tx of onychomycosis (nailbed fungus)
vignettes.a: oral terbinafine

vignettes.q: CNS fungal infection or fungemia (rigors/chills)
vignettes.a: amphotericin B

vignettes.q: Cryptococcal meningitis
vignettes.a: amphotericin B + flucytosine, then do fluconazole taper

vignettes.q: Wide-complex tachyardia
vignettes.a: ventricular tachycardia (VT)

vignettes.q: Tx for SVT
vignettes.a: vagal/carotid massage first; if doesn’t work, then adenosine

vignettes.q: Tx of SVT or VT in setting of coma / unconsciousness
vignettes.a: direct-current countershock

vignettes.q: Tx of first-degree heartblock or second-degree Mobitz I (Wenckebach)
vignettes.a: observe

vignettes.q: Tx of second-degree Mobitz II or third-degree heartblock
vignettes.a: pacemaker

vignettes.q: First-degree heartblock
vignettes.a: PR-interval >200 milliseconds

vignettes.q: Mobitz I
vignettes.a: gradually prolonging PR-interval before a QRS drops

vignettes.q: Mobitz II
vignettes.a: no gradual prolongation of PR-interval; QRS randomly drops

vignettes.q: Third-degree
vignettes.a: HR super slow at 30-40; no relation between p-waves and QRS complexes

vignettes.q: HPV vaccine when
vignettes.a: age 9-45

vignettes.q: Mom’s HepB status unknown
vignettes.a: give neonate HepB vaccine; only give immunoglobulin if mom comes back +

vignettes.q: MMR
vignettes.a: first dose at 12-15 months; second dose age 4-6 years

vignettes.q: Varicella
vignettes.a: one dose between 12-18 months

vignettes.q: Age 65 or older
vignettes.a: give Pneumo PCV13 followed by PPSV23 6-12 months later

vignettes.q: Apex to base lung changes when sitting/standing
vignettes.a: both ventilation + perfusion increase apex to base

vignettes.q: Prevention of OE in someone with constant water exposure (e.g., crew team)
vignettes.a: alcohol-acetic acid drops

vignettes.q: Tx of earwax buildup
vignettes.a: carbamide peroxide drops

vignettes.q: High BMI female + irregular menstrual cycles
vignettes.a: anovulation

vignettes.q: ovulation (anovulation)
vignettes.a: follicle retained as cyst

vignettes.q: Never give which drug to pt with Hx of uric acid stones or over-producer
vignettes.a: probenecid (uricosuric)

vignettes.q: What are rasburicase / pegloticase
vignettes.a: urate oxidase analogues → cleave uric acid directly

vignettes.q: Young kid + self-mutilation + red-orange crystals in diaper
vignettes.a: Lesch-Nyhan syndrome (X-linked)

vignettes.q: Lesch-Nyhan enzyme
vignettes.a: HGPRT deficiency

vignettes.q: Patient taking NSAID + edema; why?
vignettes.a: NSAID decreases renal blood flow → PCT increases Na reabsorption to

vignettes.q: compensate for perceived low volume status
vignettes.a: water follow sodium

vignettes.q: Leflunomide MOA
vignettes.a: dihydroorotate dehydrogenase inhibitor (pyrimidine synthesis)

vignettes.q: Any pt with red, warm, tender knee
vignettes.a: joint aspiration (arthrocentesis); septic arthritis till proven otherwise

vignettes.q: Biggest risk factor for septic arthritis
vignettes.a: abnormal joint architecture

vignettes.q: Pt group most likely to get SA
vignettes.a: those with prosthetic joints (can’t be more abnormal than fake joint)

vignettes.q: 17F had kickboxing tournament last weekend + knee is red, warm, tender
vignettes.a: arthrocentesis (SA)

vignettes.q: Kid + recurrent joint pain +/- high ESR +/- rash
vignettes.a: JRA

vignettes.q: Kid with suspected JRA has sore knee
vignettes.a: must do arthrocentesis to rule out septic arthritis

vignettes.q: Histology of DPGN
vignettes.a: wire looping capillary pattern

vignettes.q: Drugs that cause DIL
vignettes.a: Mom is HIPP → Minocycline, Hydralazine, INH, Procainamide, Penicillamine

vignettes.q: Bleeding time meaning?
vignettes.a: platelet problem

vignettes.q: PT and aPTT meaning?
vignettes.a: clotting factor problem

vignettes.q: Inheritance pattern of vWD
vignettes.a: AD

vignettes.q: Heme findings in vWD
vignettes.a: bleeding time always high; PT always normal; aPTT elevated half the time

vignettes.q: What is secondary function of vWF
vignettes.a: stabilizes factor VIII in plasma (that’s why aPTT only half time increased)

vignettes.q: vWD presentation
vignettes.a: always one platelet problem + one clotting factor problem

vignettes.q: vWD treatment
vignettes.a: desmopressin → increases release of vWF

vignettes.q: Dark urine in SS
vignettes.a: renal papillary necrosis

vignettes.q: Ticlopidine is what?
vignettes.a: ADP2Y12 blocker anti-platelet agent (clopidogrel, prasugrel, ticagrelor also)

vignettes.q: Vomiting a few hours after eating meat
vignettes.a: S. aureus preformed heat-stable toxin

vignettes.q: Tx for cerumen buildup
vignettes.a: carbamide peroxide drops

vignettes.q: Most common extra-renal location for cysts
vignettes.a: liver

vignettes.q: Dx of Cryptococcal meningitis?
vignettes.a: latex agglutination if it’s listed over India ink; mucicarmine staining (red stain) can also be done

vignettes.q: Tx for Cryptococcal meningitis
vignettes.a: amphotericin B + flucytosine, followed by fluconazole taper

vignettes.q: Most common immunodeficiency in humans
vignettes.a: IgA deficiency

vignettes.q: Motor vehicle accident (MVA) + paradoxical breathing (chest moves outward with exhalation; inward with inhalation)
vignettes.a: flail chest

vignettes.q: MVA + rib fractures + underlying infiltrates in lung + low O2 sats
vignettes.a: pulmonary contusion

vignettes.q: MVA + no rib fractures + non-central chest pain + pulmonary infiltrates underlying the painful area
vignettes.a: pulmonary contusion (resources will say “white out of the lung” for pulmonary contusion, but this is buzzywordy and never shows up on actual NBME material)

vignettes.q: MVA + pulmonary infiltrates + low O2 sats + bolus of normal saline given, resulting in worsening of O2 sats
vignettes.a: pulmonary contusion (contused lung is very sensitive to fluid overload)

vignettes.q: When you get a random ventilator Q and they want an answer
vignettes.a: “increase PEEP” almost always right

vignettes.q: Patient has improving O2 sats on ventilator; next best step?
vignettes.a: “wean from ventilator”

vignettes.q: Crater with necrotic debris on forearm + UC
vignettes.a: pyoderma gangrenosum

vignettes.q: Biopsy in Crohn
vignettes.a: non-caseating granulomas; transmural; UC you don’t see these findings

vignettes.q: Biopsy of DH
vignettes.a: IgA deposition at dermal papillae

vignettes.q: Biopsy of small bowel in lactose intolerance
vignettes.a: normal villi

vignettes.q: Dx of lactose intolerance
vignettes.a: hydrogen breath test or decreased stool pH

vignettes.q: Toxicity of acyclovir
vignettes.a: nephrotoxicity (crystal nephropathy → acyclovir stones not visible on CT)

vignettes.q: Don’t give which drugs to patients with HA
vignettes.a: ACEi (can cause angioedema)

vignettes.q: What is the product of the t(9;22)
vignettes.a: bcr/abl tyrosine kinase inhibitor

vignettes.q: Side-effect of imatinib
vignettes.a: fluid retention (edema)

vignettes.q: Inpatient Tx of MSSA
vignettes.a: IV flucloxacillin or IV cephazolin

vignettes.q: Tx of MRSA skin infection
vignettes.a: clindamycin, or TMP/SMX, or doxycycline, or linezolid → vanc has poor skin penetration

vignettes.q: Suspected incarcerated hernia in a vignette
vignettes.a: immediate groin exploration

vignettes.q: Most common cause of fever after surgery
vignettes.a: atelectasis

vignettes.q: Dx of serotonin + carcinoid syndromes
vignettes.a: urinary 5-hydroxyindole acetic acid (5-HIAA)

vignettes.q: Tx of carcinoid syndrome
vignettes.a: Tx underlying condition

vignettes.q: 12M has ongoing wheezing episodes + is on albuterol inhaler; next best step?
vignettes.a: add low-dose ICS

vignettes.q: 12M has ongoing wheezing episodes + is on albuterol inhaler; what’s most likely to decrease recurrence
vignettes.a: oral corticosteroids (student says “? I thought you said ICS was what we do next and that oral steroids are last resort” Yeah, you’re right, but they’re still most effective at decreasing recurrence. This isn’t something I’m roman

vignettes.q: MOA of nedocromil and cromolyn sodium
vignettes.a: mast cell stabilizers

vignettes.q: MOA of zileuton
vignettes.a: lipoxygenase inhibitor (enzyme that makes leukotrienes from arachidonic acid)

vignettes.q: MOA of the -lukasts
vignettes.a: leukotriene LTC, D, and E4 inhibitors. LTB4 receptor agonism is unrelated and induces neutrophilic chemotaxis (LTB4, IL-8, kallikrein, platelet-activating factor, C5a, bacterial proteins)

vignettes.q: 16M takes aspirin + gets wheezing; what are we likely to see on physical exam?
vignettes.a: answer on USMLE = nasal polyps.

vignettes.q: Kid has Hx of AERD; physician considers agent to decrease his recurrence of Sx
vignettes.a: zileuton, or -lukasts (both are correct; and only one will be listed).

vignettes.q: “Wait, why the low CO2? Aren’t you not able to breathe?”
vignettes.a: low CO2 is due to high respiratory rate; even if your bronchioles are constricted + filled with secretions, CO2 can diffuse really quickly; in contrast, O2 diffuses slowly and requires healthy airways; that’s why with a high RR, O

vignettes.q: 45F + alcoholic + increased creatine kinase
vignettes.a: rhabdomyolysis (increased risk in alcoholics)

vignettes.q: 82F + fell in her house + positive for blood on urine dipstick + negative for RBCs on urine LM
vignettes.a: rhabdomyolysis (myoglobinuria causes false-positive blood on dipstick)

vignettes.q: Woman has episiotomy posterior in the midline (vaginal incision made to allow for fetus’s head to pass through birth canal without causing vaginal laceration); if the doctor cuts too far, what will he cut into?
vignettes.a: external anal sphincter

vignettes.q: 82M + dribbling, hesitancy, interruption of urinary stream + suprapubic mass (bladder) + bacteria in the urine
vignettes.a: insert catheter first, not antibiotics

vignettes.q: 25F + 6 weeks of dysuria + anterior vaginal wall pain + urinary findings normal
vignettes.a: chronic interstitial cystitis; must have 6+ weeks of Sx in the absence of any findings; anterior vaginal wall pain sounds weird, but it’s on the obgyn NBME forms, and something to bear in mind is that a cystocele (unrelated) will

vignettes.q: Detrusor muscle
vignettes.a: contracts under parasympathetic activity via the pelvic splanchnic nerves (S2-S4); when not voiding, detrusor muscle is kept relaxed by sympathetic activity via the inferior hypogastric nerves (T10-L1).

vignettes.q: Internal urethral sphincter
vignettes.a: kept closed by sympathetic activity via inferior hypogastric nerves (T10- L1).

vignettes.q: External urethral sphincter
vignettes.a: Opened by somatic activity via the pudendal nerve (S2-4)

vignettes.q: Need to know low bicarb in pt with dehydration (or any type of shock)
vignettes.a: lactic acidosis → decreased perfusion to vital organs → decreased oxygen delivery → increased anaerobic respiration → increased lactic acid

vignettes.q: Tx for ethylene glycol and methanol toxicity
vignettes.a: fomepizole only if listed → in other words, if you get combinations with “ethanol first then fomepizole,” etc., just choose “fomepizole only” if it’s listed

vignettes.q: Paint thinner + blurry vision
vignettes.a: methanol toxicity (on one of the later Step 1 NBMEs)

vignettes.q: How is copper normally excreted by the body?
vignettes.a: through bile; defective excretory pump in Wilson

vignettes.q: Pink line tracking up the arm from the palm in 35M who burned himself recently; Dx?
vignettes.a: lymphangitis → sporotrichosis is wrong answer (can cause lymphatogenous spread)

vignettes.q: Brown recluse spider bite
vignettes.a: abdominal pain; manage symptomatically

vignettes.q: Suspected skin cancer in non-cosmetically sensitive area
vignettes.a: surgical excision

vignettes.q: Suspected skin cancer on face
vignettes.a: Mohs surgery (thin slices looking for positive margins)

vignettes.q: Suspected skin cancer on neck
vignettes.a: full-thickness biopsy

vignettes.q: Most common blood transfusion reaction?
vignettes.a: febrile non-hemolytic transfusion reaction

vignettes.q: Tx for febrile non-hemolytic transfusion reaction
vignettes.a: acetaminophen on the NBME, not prednisone

vignettes.q: What causes febrile non-hemolytic transfusion reaction?
vignettes.a: Abs against donor MHC antigens on RBCs or cytokines from leukocytes in the donor blood

vignettes.q: 72F + radical mastectomy 25 years ago + hard, raised purple lesions above the elbow; Dx?
vignettes.a: lymphangiosarcoma (Stewart-Treves syndrome) → you don’t have to agree that it’s HY, but it’s asked on the NBME → caused by chronic lymphatic insufficiency classically years after radical mastectomy.

vignettes.q: Neonate + spongy 1-cm red lesion on the chest; Dx?
vignettes.a: strawberry hemangioma

vignettes.q: Strawberry hemangioma Tx?
vignettes.a: don’t treat; will grow slightly then regress spontaneously over a few years

vignettes.q: Neonate + large vascular lesion on the leg + thrombocytopenia; what is the cause of the thrombocytopenia?
vignettes.a: “platelet sequestration.” I’ve memorized this from the NBMEs → similar to splenomegaly, which can cause thrombocytopenia from sequestration within the red pulp, the implication that the large vascular lesion of KMS is that platele

vignettes.q: “Cherry red blood/lips”
vignettes.a: CO poisoning

vignettes.q: “Brown blood” or “chocolate blood”
vignettes.a: methemoglobinemia

vignettes.q: Kid with brown blood and they ask you the mechanism (answers are “upregulation of anti-proteinase 2” or “deficiency of cytochrome reductase B5”)
vignettes.a: deficiency of cytochrome reductase B5; this is on the USMLE. I’m not with you. And if you Wiki it, you’ll see clear as day that they talk about congenital methemoglobinemia due to deficiency of cytochrome reductase B5.

vignettes.q: 22M + violaceous papules in a temporal distrubtion
vignettes.a: Sturge-Weber syndrome; student says “? I thought that was associated with Port wine stain birthmark.” Yeah, if we take a trip back to kindergarten, but you need to know it can present as cutaneous papules in a trigeminal nerve dis

vignettes.q: 16M found unconscious on floor in school bathroom + normal vitals + no eye findings + a little sluggish
vignettes.a: butane (inhalant) toxicity → caused by “dusters” / inhaling computer cleaner; this is on the USMLE!!!

vignettes.q: Tx for varicose veins
vignettes.a: compression stockings

vignettes.q: 47F has varicose veins + painful palpable cord by the ankle (is the treatment compression stockings or subcutaneous enoxaparin; both are listed)
vignettes.a: subcutaneous enoxaparin because this is superficial thrombophlebitis.

vignettes.q: Tx for arterial insufficiency
vignettes.a: exercise regimen first, THEN cilostazol (phosphodiesterase 3 inhibitor)

vignettes.q: Major side-effects of beta-blockers
vignettes.a: depression + sexual dysfunction (avoid in these patients)

vignettes.q: Major side-effect of naproxen
vignettes.a: fluid retention (edema) due to increased renal retention of sodium.

vignettes.q: What is naproxen?
vignettes.a: NSAID that the USMLE is obsessed with for some reason.

vignettes.q: Why might NSAIDs cause fluid retention / renal retention of sodium?
vignettes.a: knocking out COX → decreased prostaglandin synthesis → decreased renal afferent arteriolar dilatation → decreased renal blood flow → PCT of kidney compensates for perceived low blood volume by increasing Na reabsorption → water fo

vignettes.q: What are the four beta-blockers that decrease mortality in heart failure?
vignettes.a: Metoprolol XR (extended release) + carvedilol + nebivolol + bisoprolol → USMLE will never ask “extended-release”; they’ll just want metoprolol, but cardiologists will spasm out if you say regular metoprolol without specifying exte

vignettes.q: When do we use atenolol
vignettes.a: stage-fright

vignettes.q: MOA of baclofen
vignettes.a: GABA-B receptor agonist (USMLE loves baclofen).

vignettes.q: Tx for TA
vignettes.a: immediate IV methylprednisolone (IV steroids) to prevent blindness, then do temporal artery biopsy; do not choose biopsy before steroids.

vignettes.q: Dx of PR
vignettes.a: clinical; there’s no specific test.

vignettes.q: Oral + genital ulcers
vignettes.a: Behcet syndrome

vignettes.q: What kind of immunofluorescence on biopsy in PV vs BV?
vignettes.a: Linear in BV; net-like in PV.

vignettes.q: Tx for PV and BV
vignettes.a: oral corticosteroids

vignettes.q: Hematuria + hemoptysis + “head-itis” (mastoiditis, sinusitis, otitis, nasal septal perforation)
vignettes.a: Wegener granulomatosis

vignettes.q: Annoying new name for Wegener
vignettes.a: granulomatosis with polyangiitis

vignettes.q: Annoying new name for CS
vignettes.a: eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis

vignettes.q: 44M + hematuria + hemopytisis + head-itis
vignettes.a: Wegener

vignettes.q: What is polyarteritis nodosa
vignettes.a: medium-vessel vasculitis characterized by immune complex deposition in vascular walls and fibrinoid necrosis

vignettes.q: Polyarteritis nodosa is associated with what infection?
vignettes.a: 30% of patients are HepB positive

vignettes.q: What do you see on renal artery angiogram in PN
vignettes.a: “beads on a string” (similar to fibromuscular dysplasia, although completely unrelated diseases).

vignettes.q: Which vessels are notably not affected in PN
vignettes.a: pulmonary vessels (USMLE likes this detail).

vignettes.q: Tx for PN
vignettes.a: oral corticosteroids

vignettes.q: 17M has mononucleosis; how to best decrease risk of transmission?
vignettes.a: hand washing (“huh, I thought it was just kissing + sharing cups n stuff.” I agree with you. But the USMLE wants handwashing.

vignettes.q: Question literally asks you point-blank why a patient is given primaquine
vignettes.a: “primaquine kills hypnozoites” or “kills extra-erythrocytic forms.”

vignettes.q: How do you Tx the liver abscess?
vignettes.a: percutaneous drainage BEFORE antibiotics

vignettes.q: Fever + periorbital edema + muscle aches + went to a BBQ; Dx?
vignettes.a: Trichinella spiralis → this is a classic triad seen in trichinosis.

vignettes.q: How do you get trichinosis?
vignettes.a: bear meat (yes, Alaska is still in the United States and people hunt polar bear) or pork (pork nematode, not cestode)

vignettes.q: What is nematode vs cestode vs trematode?
vignettes.a: nematode is roundworm; cestode tapeworm; trematodes are flukes.

vignettes.q: What does T. solium cause?
vignettes.a: cysticersosis (muscle cysts) or neurocysticercosis (brain cysts)

vignettes.q: “Swiss cheese appearance” of brain in someone who traveled abroad
vignettes.a: neurocysticercosis

vignettes.q: Single cystic lesion seen on brain CT in someone who went to Mexico
vignettes.a: neurocysticercosis

vignettes.q: Tx for cysticersosis / neurocysticercosis
vignettes.a: praziquantel or albendazole (the USMLE will never give you both and make you choose between them; for anti-helminth drugs questions, the correct answer will be the only anti-helminth drug listed).

vignettes.q: Which helminth causes visceral larva migrans?
vignettes.a: Toxicara canis

vignettes.q: How do you get Loa Loa
vignettes.a: deer, horse, or mango fly

vignettes.q: Upper lobe nodular density in immunocompromised patient
vignettes.a: Aspergilloma

vignettes.q: Dx of Aspergilloma
vignettes.a: open lung biopsy

vignettes.q: 14F has massive unilateral breast mass + mom is freaking out bc her sister died of breast cancer
vignettes.a: follow-up in six months → virginal breast hypertrophy is normal during puberty.

vignettes.q: 15M has unilateral mass behind his nipple +/- tenderness of it
vignettes.a: reassurance → physiologic gynecomastia of puberty (higher androgens are aromatized to estrogens).

vignettes.q: Girl is Tanner stage 3; which of the following is true?
vignettes.a: menarche is imminent → USMLE asks this Q straight up and it’s exceedingly HY and frequent.

vignettes.q: 17F + really pad period pain + physical exam is normal
vignettes.a: primary dysmenorrhea = prostaglandin hypersecretion (PGF2alpha) → give NSAIDs.

vignettes.q: 14M is 3rd centile for height + bone age is less than chronologic age; Dx?
vignettes.a: constitutional short stature (he’ll catch up; his growth curve is just shifted to the right).

vignettes.q: 14M is 3rd centile for height; next best step in Dx?
vignettes.a: ask for information about the parents’ height trajectory → if they already say in the stem the parents are average height, answer = do bone age.

vignettes.q: Adult male is 4 feet tall + head and trunk are large in comparison to limbs; Dx?
vignettes.a: achondroplasia

vignettes.q: Tx for DT
vignettes.a: long-acting benzo (diazepam or lorazepam or chlordiazepoxide) → USMLE likes chlordiazepoxide.

vignettes.q: 42M has surgery + two days later in hospital he has restlessness + tactile/visual hallucinations; Dx?
vignettes.a: alcoholic hallucinosis → on the same spectrum as DT; Tx with long-acting benzo same as DT.

vignettes.q: MOA of buspirone
vignettes.a: serotonin receptor agonist.

vignettes.q: 2-year-old boy has writhing movements in his sleep + periventricular nodules seen on MRI of the head; what else would be seen in this pt?
vignettes.a: renal angiomyolipoma or cardiac rhabdomyoma → Dx = tuberous sclerosis (AD).

vignettes.q: Adult + heart tumor = cardiac myxoma until proven otherwise (ball-in-valve tumor in the left atrium
vignettes.a: causes a diastolic rumble that abates when patient is positioned in an unusual way, e.g., on his right side while leaning diagonally).

vignettes.q: 32F + pedal + forearm edema after commencing anti-hypertensive agent; Dx?
vignettes.a: fluid retention / edema caused by dihydropyridine CCB (e.g., nifedipine) → really HY side-effect of d-CCBs!

vignettes.q: CNS disturbance due to an electrolyte problem
vignettes.a: high or low sodium; high calcium

vignettes.q: Cardiac disturbance (arrhythmia) due to an electrolyte problem
vignettes.a: high or low potassium or calcium

vignettes.q: Low calcium or potassium not responding to supplementation
vignettes.a: check serum magnesium (low Mg can cause low Ca and K refractory to supplementation

vignettes.q: Who gets low Mg
vignettes.a: alcoholics (dietary deficiency; nothing malabsorptive or magic; they just drink too much and fill up on EtOH bc it’s 7kcal/gram).

vignettes.q: MOA of bosentan
vignettes.a: endothelin-1 receptor antagonist

vignettes.q: Which of the following is true in the above 28F?
vignettes.a: “increased vascular expression of endothelin 1.” → if you know bosentan can treat, then inferring this is easy.

vignettes.q: 22M takes a drug + gets nystagmus + bellicosity (wants to fight)
vignettes.a: PCP.

vignettes.q: 2-year-old boy running + playing with 8-year-old sister + they were holding hands and he fell + now he holds arm pronated by his side; Dx?
vignettes.a: nursemaid’s elbow → radial head subluxation

vignettes.q: Tx for nursemaid’s elbow
vignettes.a: hyperpronation OR gentle supination (both are correct answers; only one will be listed).

vignettes.q: Kid falls on outstretched arm + pain over anatomical snuffbox; Dx?
vignettes.a: scaphoid fracture

vignettes.q: What part of the clavicle gets fractured easiest?
vignettes.a: middle-third

vignettes.q: Tx for cubital tunnel syndrome
vignettes.a: elbow splint

vignettes.q: Perineal gangrene in 50M diabetic
vignettes.a: Fournier gangrene → do surgical debridement.

vignettes.q: Neonate + strange hereditary disease + mutation analysis shows homozygous gene deletion; what’s the most likely inheritance pattern?
vignettes.a: autosomal recessive; some students get caught up by saying, “Wait, we’re supposed to know the inheritance pattern of this weird disease?” No. It’s the fact that they say homozygous deletion, without mentioning that either parent h

vignettes.q: Patient takes nedocromil for seasonal allergies; what’s the MOA of this drug?
vignettes.a: blocks release of autacoids from cellular storage; student says ?; mast cell stabilizers like nedocromil and cromolyn sodium prevent the release of histamine, which acts as an autacoid, which means it’s a biologic molecule that ac

vignettes.q: How many kilocalories in one gram of fat, carbs, protein, and ethanol?
vignettes.a: 9 kcal/g of fat; 4 for both carbs and protein; 7 for ethanol; USMLE Q will give you some nutrition Q where you have to do math, and it will rely on you knowing this nutritional info to get the Q right.

vignettes.q: 20F + recurrent Staph infections + deficiency of CD18; what mechanism best explains this condition?
vignettes.a: failure of emigration of phagocytes to inflamed tissues; leukocyte adhesion deficiency is caused by deficiency of LFA-1/CD18 integrin, which is required for diapedesis of leukocytes to sites of infection; result is recurrent infec

vignettes.q: 54F + treated with anti-platelet agent that prevents platelets from interacting with fibrinogen; what’s the agent?
vignettes.a: abciximab → monoclonal antibody against glycoproteins IIb/IIIa on platelets; these glycoproteins carry out aggregation and are normally bridged by fibrinogen; abciximab is a fibrinogen analogue; don’t confuse aggregation (platelet

vignettes.q: 34F + receives phentolamine; what intracellular effect is expected?
vignettes.a: ↓ phospholipase C activity; phentolamine is a1 antagonist; a1 is coupled to a G-alpha-q G-protein. Agonism will phospholipase C activity, which will ↑ IP3 and ↑ DAG; therefore antagonism will ↓ phospholipase C activity, ↓ IP3, and

vignettes.q: 25M + has facial nerve and optic nerve on left damaged in car accident; why does he regenerate facial movement over time but not vision?
vignettes.a: optic nerve is myelinated by oligodendrocytes; oligodendrocyte-myelinated nerves of CNS have limited regenerative capacity compared to Schwann cell-myelinated nerves of the PNS; facial nerve is myelinated by Schwann cells.

vignettes.q: Woman gets toxoplasmosis but cats isn’t listed as an answer; where did she get it from?
vignettes.a: pork; can also be written as just simply “delicatessen meats”; both answers on offline NBMEs.

vignettes.q: 50F + weight loss + progressive shortness of breath + CXR shows pleural-based mass encasing the lungs; what kind of cells are this patient’s malignant cells derived from?
vignettes.a: mesothelial cells; mesothelioma will classically present with pleural and/or supradiaphragmatic plaques; if shown a gross specimen, mesothelioma will appear to surround the lungs circumferentially, rather than appearing as an isol

vignettes.q: What is the role of IkB in relation to NFkB?
vignettes.a: “releases NFkB after undergoing phosphorylation”; USMLE also wants you to know that corticosteroids ↓ NFkB signaling in leukocytes.

vignettes.q: 29M + lancinating/stabbing pain in cheek lasting several seconds + happens spontaneously; Q asks location of problem; answer = pons; unusual answer, since trigeminal neuralgia is a peripheral mechanism, but CN
vignettes.a: Do not confuse trigeminal neuralgia of the V1 distribution with cluster headache; the latter will occur usually during sleep and will last up to half hour; details such as lacrimation and rhinorrhea are HY but too easy and often o

vignettes.q: 23F + relaxing after coming back from a run; which of the following describes her changes in diastole and systole as her heart rate returns to normal?
vignettes.a: diastole increases more than systole; the Q can also be asked as the inverse: that is, as HR increases, diastole shortens more than systole; the learning point is that the slower the heart rate, the greater the proportion of time

vignettes.q: 34F + chest pain that does not change with position + chest pain worse with palpation; diagnosis?
vignettes.a: costochondritis; even though it doesn’t change with position, it worsens with palpation.

vignettes.q: 40F + found in street with hypothermia + rewarmed in hospital + picture is shown of her feet and they’re red; what electrolyte are we most worried about?
vignettes.a: hyperkalemia → reperfusion injury causes oxygen radicals that increase the risk of rhabdo, especially in alcoholics.

vignettes.q: 82F + found in her house by the staircase; urine blood is 2+; RBCs on urine light microscopy are 3-4 per high-power field; diagnosis?
vignettes.a: rhabdomyolysis; classic finding is false-positive blood on urine dipstick; USMLE can give 3-4 RBCs/hpf as false-positive.

vignettes.q: Question gives 40s male with duodenal ulcers caused by H. pylori. Following antibiotic treatment, they ask what lifestyle variable is most likely to promote healing of ulcers
vignettes.a: smoking cessation. Reducing alcohol intake can also help, but I’ve seen smoking cessation as answer on NBME, where they don’t have abstinence from alcohol as an answer.

vignettes.q: 11F + rhinoconjunctivitis past month; Q asks what to ask parents about
vignettes.a: “recent pets in household”; if recent allergy-like presentation in a patient with no prior Hx, inquire about pets.

vignettes.q: 50M + diabetic + high LDL + low HDL + high BMI; Q asks best way to decrease long-term complications in this patient
vignettes.a: “good glycemic control”; generic answer, similar to smoking cessation, but this is HY.

vignettes.q: 65M + long history of alcoholism and smoking + pulsatile mass in epigastrium; Q wants to know #1 way to have prevented this patient’s condition → answer = smoking cessation; the demographic that classically get
vignettes.a: Guidelines vary on screening for AAA, but updated literature says both men and women 65- 75 who have ever-smoked should get a one-off abdominal ultrasound to screen for AAA. Lower thresholds can be used in patients with family his

vignettes.q: 14M + hits head while skateboarding + loses consciousness briefly + head CT shows biconvex-shaped bleed; what is major risk factor
vignettes.a: head temporal trauma resulting in rupture of middle meningeal artery.

vignettes.q: 50F + has diabetic foot ulcer; Q asks how this condition could have best been prevented
vignettes.a: wearing comfortable-fitting shoes; wrong answer is nightly foot checks. Both are important to prevent foot ulcers, but if both choices are listed together, choose wearing comfortable-fitting shoes.

vignettes.q: 65M + long-standing diabetes + diarrhea; Dx + risk factor?
vignettes.a: diabetic neuropathy to bowel affecting hypogastric nerves (loss of anti-peristalsis sympathetic nerves → causes too much peristalsis).

vignettes.q: 65M + long-standing diabetes + constipation; Dx + risk factor?
vignettes.a: diabetic neuropathy to bowel affecting pelvic splanchnic nerves (loss of pro-peristalsis parasympathetic nerves).

vignettes.q: 27F + painful thyroid + low uptake of radioiodine on scan; Dx + risk factor?
vignettes.a: subacute granulomatous thyroiditis (aka deQuervain); risk factor is viral infection; answer on USMLE for tender/painful thyroid.

vignettes.q: 60M + had gastrectomy performed 6 months ago + now has neuropathy; Dx + risk factor?
vignettes.a: B12 deficiency due to gastrectomy (loss of parietal cells which produce intrinsic factor).

vignettes.q: 24F + vegan + high MCV + hyper-segmented neutrophil on smear; Dx + risk factor?
vignettes.a: B12 deficiency due to veganism (can also be strict vegetarianism).

vignettes.q: 34F + giving birth + fetal anterior shoulder caught behind mother’s pubic symphysis; Dx + risk factor?
vignettes.a: shoulder dystocia; risk factor is fetal macrosomia due to maternal diabetes (causes big baby). This can cause clavicular fracture in the newborn.

vignettes.q: Above 34F + experiences excessive vaginal bleeding despite McRobert’s maneuver to deliver in setting of shoulder dystocia; Dx + risk factor? → vaginal laceration due to macrosomia from maternal diabetes.
vignettes.a: In short: maternal diabetes causes fetal macrosomia → results in shoulder dystocia → results in fetal clavicular fracture + maternal vaginal laceration during delivery.

vignettes.q: 30F + 38 weeks’ gestation + fever 103F + CVA tenderness; Dx + risk factor?
vignettes.a: pyelonephritis; uterus can compress ureters in third trimester, increasing risk for pyelo; in addition, progesterone slows ureteral peristalsis.

vignettes.q: 35F + pregnant + abnormal AFP measurement; risk factor?
vignettes.a: dating error is most common cause of abnormal AFP measurement; next best step is fetal ultrasound to get correct dates (i.e., crown-rump length); re-measure AFP is wrong answer (the lab result wasn’t wrong, just the ultrasound dat

vignettes.q: 40F + pregnant + low AFP + low estriol + high b-hCG + high inhibin A; Dx + risk factor?
vignettes.a: Down syndrome due to increased maternal age.

vignettes.q: 4M + recent gastroenteritis + now has diarrhea after meals; Dx + risk factor?
vignettes.a: lactose intolerance; risk factor is recent GI viral infection; the latter can cause transient lactose intolerance due to sloughing of brush border (hence losing disaccharidase).

vignettes.q: 4M + small, shrunken kidney + tubular atrophy seen on biopsy; Dx + risk factor?
vignettes.a: chronic pyelonephritis; major risk factor is recurrent acute pyelo, either from vesicoureteral reflux or posterior urethral valves (can be written on NBME as “congenital urethral obstruction”).

vignettes.q: 45M + various medium-sized arteries with fibrinoid necrosis and segmental, beaded, “rosary sign”; diagnosis + risk factor?
vignettes.a: polyarteritis nodosa; major risk factor is hepatitis B (30% of patients with PA are seropositive for HepB).

vignettes.q: 3F + consumes bottle of pills left open in medicine cabinet at home + has blood in the stool + the pills are visible on abdominal x-ray. What are the arrows (i.e., ↑, ↓, or ↔) for pH, HCO3-, CO2, and anion-gap?
vignettes.a: ↓ pH, ↓ HCO3- , ↓ CO2, ↑ anion-gap. — Diagnosis is acute iron toxicity. • Iron tablets are one of the MUDPILES high anion-gap metabolic acidoses. • (MUDPILES) → Methanol toxicity, Uremia (renal failure), DKA, Phenformin (weird dru

vignettes.q: Tx for aspirin toxicity
vignettes.a: bicarb (increased excretion through urinary alkalinization)

vignettes.q: Tx of urge incontinence
vignettes.a: oxybutynin (muscarinic cholinergic antagonist) or mirabegron (beta-3 agonist)

vignettes.q: Tx for overflow incontinence in diabetes
vignettes.a: bethanacol (muscarinic cholinergic agonist)

vignettes.q: “Hot feels cold; cold feels hot” (temperature dysesthesia)
vignettes.a: ciguatera toxicity → toxin blocks sodium channels → caused by consumption of reef fish (mahimahi, Spanish mackerel, etc.)

vignettes.q: Pt with no prior Hx of atopy/asthma + eats meaty fish in sketch location (e.g., Bali) + develops dyspnea + allergic-like reaction
vignettes.a: scombroid, not seafood allergy → histidine decarboxylase in decaying fish convert histidine to histamine → allergic-like reaction (often misdiagnosed as allergy)

vignettes.q: Pt gets allergic-like reaction after eating shellfish
vignettes.a: shellfish allergy, not scombroid (students get all trigger-happy about scombroid after learning about something new, weird, and cool, but if on the USMLE they say shellfish, it’s shellfish allergy, not scombroid)

vignettes.q: Tx for HA
vignettes.a: danazol (synthetic androgen receptor partial agonist that causes liver to make more C1EI)

vignettes.q: Overflow incontinence
vignettes.a: answer in diabetes and BPH → neurogenic bladder caused by myelin damage from sorbitol (glucose enters myelin, causing osmotic damage); in BPH, merely due to outlet obstruction → leads to detrusor burnout; in overflow incontinence,

vignettes.q: 22M + on anti-depressant med + has suprapubic mass + face is hot and red; which drug is he on?
vignettes.a: amitriptyline (any TCA is answer); TCAs also have nasty anti-cholinergic side-effects → opposite of DUMBBELSS (refers to cholinergic side-effects) → diarrhea, urination, myosis, bradycardia, bronchoconstriction, excitation of skel

vignettes.q: 30F + going on a plane + receives diphenhydramine to prevent motion sickness; what receptor is responsible for anti-motion sickness in this patient?
vignettes.a: anti-muscarinic; diphenhydramine and chlorpheniramine are first-generation H1-blockers with nasty anti-cholinergic side-effects; muscarinic receptor blockade ameliorates feelings of motion sickness; H1 will not be listed as an ans

vignettes.q: 50M + swollen big toe + smoker + works on farm in California + drinks home-distilled liquor; Q wants to know biggest risk factor for this patient’s condition
vignettes.a: home-distilled liquor; patient has podagra (gout of big toe) from alcohol; the fact that it’s home-distilled doesn’t mean lead poisoning in this context, but this is on NBME. Smoking doesn’t cause gout; farming can be risk factor

vignettes.q: 23F + works on fruit farm + doesn’t wear mask + doesn’t wear gloves + develops pinpoint pupils and salivation; Q wants to know what would most likely have prevented this patient’s condition
vignettes.a: wearing gloves; wrong answer = face mask; organophosphate poisoning occurs through the skin, not inhalation (on NBME).

vignettes.q: 16F + consumed bottle of pills in suicide attempt + now has severe elevation in ALT and AST; what is risk factor for this presentation
vignettes.a: acetaminophen toxicity; antidote = N-acetylcysteine.

vignettes.q: Gross motor:
vignettes.a: Head up at 3 months (can support his/her own head unassisted). Turn over front to back at 4-5 months. Sits up at 6 months. Crawls by 9 months. Stands/walks alongside sofa at 10-11 months. Walks at 12-15 months.

vignettes.q: Fine Motor:
vignettes.a: Pincer grasp at 9 months. Stacks 3, 6, 9 blocks at age 1, 2, 3, respectively. Copies circle at 3-4 years. Copies square at 4-5 years. Copies triangle at 5-6 years.

vignettes.q: Language development:
vignettes.a: “Mama” and “dada” by 1 year. Recognizes own name by 1 year. 2-word sentences at age 2. 900-word vocabulary at age 3.

vignettes.q: Social:
vignettes.a: Social smile at 2-3 months. Stranger anxiety at 6-9 months. Separation anxiety at 9-14 months. Parallel play age 2-3 (kids play side by side); cooperative play age 3-4. Imaginary friends are normal at age 4-6. (USMLE likes this. N

vignettes.q: "Rule of 4s"
vignettes.a: After a patient is started on an antipsychotic, a general trend is seen in terms of the onset of particular symptoms. The time frame is not strict/rigid; use it as a general trend – i.e., acute dystonia wouldn't just start at 4 mo

vignettes.q: Acute dystonia at 4 hours
vignettes.a: torticollis, oculogyric crisis, muscle rigidity without fever.

vignettes.q: Parkinsonism at 4 weeks
vignettes.a: akinesia / bradykinesia.

vignettes.q: Tardive dyskinesia at 4 months
vignettes.a: abnormal facial movements (notably tongue).

vignettes.q: Patient on atypical + gets TD; Tx?
vignettes.a: stop the atypical and give another atypical. (Just stop the drug and switch to yet another atypical.)

vignettes.q: Mechanism for NMS is: the ryanodine channel, which allows calcium to move from the sarcoplasmic reticulum into the cytosol, gets stuck open, so ↑ calcium moves into the cytoplasm. The cell then needs to use a l
vignettes.a: fever.

vignettes.q: 12M + sore throat + new-onset tic; Dx?
vignettes.a: PANDAS (Pediatric Autoimmune Neuropsychiatric Disorder

vignettes.q: 65M + given IV methylprednisolone for temporal arteritis + develops confusion + visual hallucinations; Dx?
vignettes.a: “corticosteroid-induced psychotic disorder”; astute student says, “I thought that happens with high doses over longer periods of time.” → response: yeah, but Psych NBME has it occurring after a one-off dose in a patient. Bottom li

vignettes.q: 82M + confusion + on various meds; Dx? → various answers on NBME are: “discontinuation of anticholinergic medications”; “discontinuation of diphenhydramine” (1st gen H1 blocker); “discontinuation of amitriptyli
vignettes.a: Anti-cholinergic (anti-muscarinic) Anti-alpha-1-adrenergic Anti-H1-histaminergic

vignettes.q: “What do you mean by anticholinergic effects of meds?”
vignettes.a: Start with knowing that DUMBBELSS is a mnemonic for cholinergic effects: Diarrhea, Urination, Miosis (pupillary constriction), Bradycardia, Bronchoconstriction, Excitation (neuromuscular), Lacrimation, Salivation, Sweating → so by

vignettes.q: “What do you mean by anti-alpha-1-adrenergic?”
vignettes.a: alpha-1 normally constricts peripheral arterioles → anti-alpha-1 effects can precipitate orthostatic hypotension + fainting.

vignettes.q: “What do you mean by anti-H1-histaminergic effects?”
vignettes.a: sedation.

vignettes.q: 8M + develops visual hallucinations after starting on over-the-counter cold med provided by his mother; Dx?
vignettes.a: anticholinergic delirium caused by diphenhydramine or dextromethorphan (anti- tussive opioid).

vignettes.q: 82M + urinary hesitancy + interrupted stream + taking amitriptyline; next best step?
vignettes.a: discontinue amitriptyline.

vignettes.q: 25M + started on new psych med + is now hot and dry; Dx?
vignettes.a: anticholinergic effects of TCA.

vignettes.q: 35F + family member Dx with breast cancer + says she can’t sleep; Q asks which med to give
vignettes.a: answer on Psych NBME = clonazepam → benzo OK for acute Tx of insomnia; never prescribe chronically.

vignettes.q: 35M + recently divorced + stressed + insomnia; which med to give: answers are SSRI, antipsychotic, and zolpidem; answer = zolpidem
vignettes.a: non-benzo zolpidem may be used short-term for insomnia. Take home point is be aware both benzo + non-benzo can be used acutely for insomnia.

vignettes.q: 52F + 8-week Hx of progressive confusion and memory loss + myoclonus; Dx?
vignettes.a: Creutzfeldt-Jakob syndrome (prion disease).

vignettes.q: 65M + visual hallucinations + bradykinesia + gradual cognitive decline; Dx?
vignettes.a: Lewy body dementia.

vignettes.q: 65M + pulls his pants down when guests come over to the house + apathy; Dx?
vignettes.a: frontotemporal dementia (Pick disease) → characterized by apathy, disinhibition, personality change.

vignettes.q: 65M + Parkinsonism + axial dystonia; Dx?
vignettes.a: progressive supranuclear palsy (student had this on the USMLE).

vignettes.q: 65M + wet, wobbly, wacky + Parkinsonism; Dx?
vignettes.a: normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH) → urinary incontinence, ataxia, cognitive dysfunction; key point to make here is the Parkinsonism. Wiki it yourself, you’ll see.

vignettes.q: Mechanism for incontinence in NPH?
vignettes.a: “failure to inhibit the voiding reflex.”

vignettes.q: Area of the brain affected in Huntington?
vignettes.a: answer on shelf = caudate nucleus.

vignettes.q: 22M + hyperoralism + hyperphagia + docility; Dx?
vignettes.a: Kluver-Bucy syndrome → bilateral amygdala lesions.

vignettes.q: Cause of Kluver-Bucy syndrome?
vignettes.a: most often due to HSV encephalitis.

vignettes.q: 49M + Down syndrome + forgetfulness; which part of brain is affected?
vignettes.a: nucleus basalis of Maynert → high-density of cholinergic neurons (basal forebrain) → affected in Alzheimer (early-onset in Down).

vignettes.q: Where in the brain is there high amount of norepinephrine production?
vignettes.a: locus coeruleus (pons).

vignettes.q: Where in the brain are there high amounts of serotonergic neurons?
vignettes.a: raphe nucleus (medial reticular formation).

vignettes.q: Pharm Tx for Alzheimer?
vignettes.a: acetylcholinesterase inhibitors first (donepezil, galantamine, rivastigmine); sometimes Q will ask for mechanism, and answer = “cholinergic”; for more advanced disease try NMDA (glutamate) receptor antagonist (memantine).

vignettes.q: 74M + MMSE 22/30 + avoids eye contact + weight loss + low mood; DX and Tx?
vignettes.a: pseudodementia → Tx = sertraline (SSRI), not donepezil.

vignettes.q: Main way to differentiate pseudodementia from dementia?
vignettes.a: pseudodementia is depression that presents as cognitive decline; vignette may describe weight loss or gain, avoidance of eye contact, low mood, and/or tearing up during interview; vignette may also mention poor performance on the

vignettes.q: Other notable causes of reversible cognitive decline?
vignettes.a: hypothyroidism, B12 deficiency, neurosyphilis, neuro Lyme.

vignettes.q: 48F + BMI 26 + cholesterol elevated + HR 55 + creatine kinase (CK) elevated; Dx?
vignettes.a: hypothyroidism → check serum TSH; hypothyroid myopathy can cause proximal muscle weakness + elevated serum CK.

vignettes.q: 81F + cooks own meals since husband passed away + seems depressed + various non-acute neurologic findings; next best step?
vignettes.a: assess suicide risk (this answer is basically always correct if it’s listed).

vignettes.q: 81F + memory decline; next best step after assessing suicide risk?
vignettes.a: Mini-Mental State Exam (MMSE).

vignettes.q: 81F + cooks own meals since husband passed away + seems depressed + various non-acute neurologic findings + MMSE is 25/30 + no suicidal ideation; next best step?
vignettes.a: check serum B12 → subacute combined degeneration (SCD) = pattern of neurologic dysfunction seen in B12 deficiency.

vignettes.q: Which three spinal tracts are involved in SCD?
vignettes.a: lateral corticospinal, spinocerebellar, dorsal columns → just remember that the spinothalamic is not involved.

vignettes.q: 68M + started on various medications 8 weeks ago for low ejection fraction heart failure + now has depressed mood; most likely cause?
vignettes.a: depression caused by beta-blocker.

vignettes.q: Nocturnal enuresis; when is it pathologic?
vignettes.a: after age 5.

vignettes.q: 6M + nocturnal enuresis; next best step? USMLE / NBME / shelf wants the following order:
vignettes.a: Behavioral answer first; e.g., spend more time with child; decrease overt stressors as much as possible. If the above not an answer, do star chart (positive reinforcement therapy; i.e., don’t wet the bed and get a star; get 5 star

vignettes.q: Patient wants to commit suicide; next best step?
vignettes.a: admit to hospital involuntarily.

vignettes.q: Acutely suicidal patient + you need to admit him/her; what do you say?
vignettes.a: “how would you feel about entering hospital?”

vignettes.q: 33M + robbed at gunpoint two days ago + now is mute and not responding to questions; Tx?
vignettes.a: benzo (lorazepam) → catatonia secondary to adverse stimulus.

vignettes.q: 39F + >6-month Hx of multiple worries (i.e., career, marriage, kids going to college, etc.) + no overt mood or psychotic Sx; Dx?
vignettes.a: generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) → Dx is >6 months of general worries without lack of specific stressor.

vignettes.q: Tx of GAD?
vignettes.a: cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and/or SSRI; second-line pharm agent is buspirone, which is a serotonin receptor agonist; USMLE wants you to know buspirone + its mechanism, but also remember that it’s not first-line for GAD; SS

vignettes.q: 33M + ingested substance + high RR + now has calcium oxalate urolithiasis; Dx?
vignettes.a: ethylene glycol toxicity → causes calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis; high RR is due to respiratory compensation for high-anion gap metabolic acidosis (MUDPILES).

vignettes.q: 16M + found on floor in school bathroom + brought into hospital + sluggish + pupils and vitals normal; which drug/substance did he do?
vignettes.a: butane (inhalant toxicity); this is HY!

vignettes.q: 14M + cognitive decline over a few months + ataxia; which drug/substance did he do?
vignettes.a: glue, not alcohol → 14 is too young to get alcohol-induced cerebellar ataxia.

vignettes.q: 22M takes a drug + gets nystagmus + bellicosity (wants to fight)
vignettes.a: PCP.

vignettes.q: 22M + sluggish patient + has angiogram performed (for some reason) that shows decreased cerebral blood flow; drug that was taken?
vignettes.a: cocaine; this question is on USMLE. Cocaine is known to cause vasoconstriction, i.e., placental abruption, coronary vasospasm; apparently that extends to cerebral blood flow on the exam.

vignettes.q: 16F + injected conjunctivae + has paranoia; Dx + Tx?
vignettes.a: marijuana intoxication; observation.

vignettes.q: Tx for OCD on shelf?
vignettes.a: SSRI (i.e., sertraline).

vignettes.q: 23M + hearing voices for 6 weeks + staying up all night for 4 weeks; Dx?
vignettes.a: schizoaffective disorder → Dx is >2 weeks of psychotic disorder in the absence of mood disorder.

vignettes.q: What are the important timeframes for schizophrenia vs schizophreniform vs brief psychotic disorder?
vignettes.a: brief psychotic disorder is < 1 month; schizophreniform is 1-6 months; schizophrenia is >6 months of psychosis.

vignettes.q: If brain imaging performed in schizophrenic patient, what would be seen?
vignettes.a: enlargement of the third and lateral ventricles.

vignettes.q: Major characteristic in psych vignettes that suggests psychotic disorder?
vignettes.a: auditory hallucinations; in contrast, visual hallucinations are non-specific and seen frequently in drug use (alcohol, amphetamines, marijuana, etc.).

vignettes.q: What is bipolar I vs II?
vignettes.a: bipolar I is worse than II; both will have cycling episodes of mania and depression, but bipolar I will often tell you there’s Hx of hospitalization, or losing one’s job, friends, or relationships (socio-occupational dysfunction),

vignettes.q: Tx for bipolar?
vignettes.a: lithium or valproic acid to start.

vignettes.q: Adverse effects of lithium and valproic acid?
vignettes.a: lithium causes Ebstein anomaly in pregnancy (atrialization of right ventricle in fetus); also tremor and thyroid dysfunction; valproic acid notoriously causes neural tube defects.

vignettes.q: What is cyclothymia vs dysthymia?
vignettes.a: cyclothymia is >2 years of swinging low + elevated moods, but never meets the thresholds for bipolar + never has true depressive episode. Dysthymia is >2 years of low moods not ever meeting thresholds for MDD.

vignettes.q: When is delusional disorder the answer?
vignettes.a: one, fixed, non-bizarre delusion + no other mood or psychotic Sx; presentation will often be patient with mistrust + suspects coworkers and neighbors are attempting to undermine her work or are stealing from her. If the vignette s
